about: THE CHRONICLE OF 793-1066 - real, dated events from the sources of the time, which the game's log shows as the date passes and which drive the world: raids on their days, laws taking effect, ports and routes opening and closing, famines, hard winters, fairs, wars. Rules: real events only, each with its sources (the work and its year entry, e.g. ARF 808, ASC (D/E) 793, AU 795.3, Theophanes AM 6305; see abbreviations). Titles, effects and notes are in our own plain words, not quoted from modern translations; short Latin or Old English terms are kept. All dates are Julian. 'date' and 'precision' (day, month, season, year) give what the sources allow; 'fire' is the day the game shows the entry (day: that day; month: the 1st; season: mid-season, 15 Apr / 15 Jul / 15 Oct, and winters as set; year: 1 July unless the annal's order puts it elsewhere). Where sources disagree, or a day is reconstructed (feasts turned into days, AH and AM years, the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle's two-year slip c. 754-845, the Annales Mosellani running a year behind, the ARF starting its year at Christmas), the note says so; (?) marks a doubt. certainty: sure / likely / uncertain. ports: port ids from ports_793.json where the event happens at or near that port. regions: trade regions from goods_793.json that the event touches; an empty list means news only - seen everywhere (eclipses) or off the map ('area' names where). realm: the realm (ids as in ports_793.json) the event touches as a whole - a ruler's change or a realm-wide law; realm 'franks' already lists every Frankish region. effect: a plain hint for the game. end: when the state it sets ends. Entries before the start (21 June 793) are the backstory the log shows at the beginning. Up to 814 it follows the annals closely; from 815 to 1066 it keeps to the broad main points and the notable events (raids on the trading places, the kings and wars that changed who held the ports, laws, tolls and coins, great storms and winters, the voyages west and east), with later sources (sagas, chronicles written long after) marked uncertain or noted. Edit freely: the game reads this file.

entries.title: Great famine in Burgundy, Francia, Italy, Gothia and Provence; many die
entries.effect: famine across the Frankish lands: grain very dear, deaths, people sell what they have
entries.note: Ann. Mosell. (a year behind) date its start to the harvest of 792 and tell of cannibalism; Moissac adds Italy, Gothia and Provence. Eased by the harvest of 794.

entries.title: Ealdorman Sicga, slayer of King Aelfwald, dies
entries.effect: a leading Northumbrian faction loses its head
entries.note: viii kal. Mar. HR: he died by his own hand (?); his body was taken to Lindisfarne on 23 April.

entries.title: Famine in Benevento: the Frankish army under Pippin and Louis must eat meat in Lent
entries.effect: famine in southern Italy: grain very dear; Frankish army foraging
entries.note: Sent in winter 792/793; Lent 793 ran 20 Feb-6 Apr (Easter 7 Apr).

entries.title: Blood-red rain falls from the roof of St Peter's church at York in Lent
entries.effect: omen at eoforwic: unease
entries.note: Lent 793 ran 20 Feb-6 Apr. Told by Alcuin to King Aethelred after the Lindisfarne raid: it fell from the north side in clear weather.

entries.title: False grain seen in fields, woods and marshes that could be touched but not eaten
entries.effect: panic in the famine; tithes urged
entries.note: Frankfurt (794) c. 25 recalls the empty ears 'eaten by demons' in the year of the famine.

entries.title: Portents over Northumbria: flashes of light, whirlwinds and fiery dragons in the sky
entries.effect: omen in Northumbria: fear of famine and raids
entries.note: No day given; the ASC orders them: portents, then famine, then the raid.

entries.title: Great famine in Northumbria
entries.effect: famine in Northumbria: grain dear at eoforwic and the coastal monasteries
entries.note: The ASC places it after the portents and before the Lindisfarne raid.

entries.title: Constantine VI crushes the revolt of the Armeniakon theme
entries.effect: Byzantine east unsettled
entries.note: Theophanes puts the fight at Pentecost, which fell on 26 May 793.

entries.title: Heathen seamen sack the monastery of Lindisfarne, killing and carrying off monks
entries.effect: raid on lindisfarena: church treasure taken, monks killed, drowned or enslaved; Northumbrian coast hostile in the sailing season
entries.note: ASC D/E read vi id. Ian. (8 January), usually emended to vi id. Iun. (8 June); Symeon gives vii id. Iun. (7 June). The raid is certain; the day is 7 or 8 June.

entries.title: News: Count Theoderic's force wiped out by Saxons in Rüstringen by the Weser
entries.effect: Weser mouth and Rüstringen hostile; East Frisian coast unsafe for Frankish ships
entries.note: The revised ARF gives the news in 793, reaching Charles at Regensburg. Ann. S. Amandi put a slaughter of Franks by the sea in 792, Ann. Mosell. troops coming by ship through Frisia betrayed in 792: the defeat itself was probably 792 (?).

entries.title: Offa's heavier, broader penny replaces the lighter Mercian coinage (c. 792/3)
sources: numismatic: Offa's heavy coinage (Blackburn & Grierson, MEC 1; Chick, The Coinage of Offa)
entries.effect: coin: new heavy penny at lundenwic, in Kent and East Anglia
entries.note: Dated by coin study only, not by an annal; often linked with the Frankish coin reform of 793/794.

entries.title: Artri son of Cathal ordained king of Munster; the law of Ailbe proclaimed in Munster
entries.effect: new king of Munster; law: Cain Ailbe in Munster

entries.title: Law of Coman proclaimed in the three Connachta
entries.effect: law: Cain Chomain in Connacht

entries.title: Cordoban army burns the suburbs of Narbonne and attacks Gerona
entries.effect: Septimanian coast raided; Narbonne disrupted; captives and booty taken to Cordoba
entries.note: Arab sources give AH 177 (17 Apr 793-9 Apr 794). Hisham struck while Charles was busy with the Avars.

entries.title: Arab raiders take the Byzantine frontier forts of Kamachon and Thebasa
entries.effect: eastern frontier of Byzantium pushed back

entries.title: Count William of Toulouse beaten by the Cordoban army on the Orbieu
entries.place: river Orbieu (Oliveius), between Narbonne and Carcassonne
entries.effect: Frankish march beaten: land route to Spain closed; Septimania open to raiders this season
entries.note: Moissac names the stream Oliveius: Orbieu or Orbiel (?). Heavy Frankish losses; the raiders went home with booty.

entries.title: Offa raises St Alban's relics and founds St Albans abbey (St Albans tradition)
entries.effect: new pilgrim abbey north of lundenwic
entries.note: Offa's foundation is accepted; the 1 August date and the story come from later St Albans tradition.

entries.title: Alcuin writes from Francia, offering to ask Charles about the Lindisfarne captives
entries.effect: possible ransom of Lindisfarne captives through the Frankish court; Wearmouth-Jarrow warned
entries.note: Ep. 20: Alcuin will ask when the king is back from campaign; ep. 19 warns the monks of Wearmouth-Jarrow, who live by the sea.

entries.title: Saxons and East Frisians in revolt: churches burned, priests driven out
entries.effect: route through Saxony and the Frisian coast east of the Lauwers hostile
entries.note: The revolt began in 792; news of a fresh breach reached Charles at the canal in autumn 793. These routes are best treated as hostile from the start.

entries.title: Charles digs a ship canal (Fossa Carolina) between Altmühl and Rednitz; rain defeats it
entries.effect: no through waterway Danube-Main-Rhine; boats still hauled overland
entries.note: Revised ARF: about 2,000 paces long and 300 feet wide; the banks slid back each night.

entries.title: Charles brings his boats down the Rednitz and Main; Christmas at Würzburg
entries.effect: royal river fleet on the Main; court winters at Frankfurt
entries.note: Ann. Guelf.: the ships were dragged overland and by river to Frankfurt, where he wintered.

entries.title: Offa has King Aethelberht of East Anglia beheaded and takes East Anglia
entries.effect: East Anglia (gipeswic, dommoc) passes under Mercian rule
entries.note: The ASC year is two too early here; the later cult keeps 20 May as the day (?).

entries.title: Synod of Frankfurt fixes grain and bread prices and a new public modius
entries.effect: law: grain capped per new modius - oats 1 d., barley 2, rye 3, wheat 4; 12 two-pound wheat loaves for 1 d.; royal grain cheaper; lords must keep their people from starving
entries.note: The synod met on 1 June (Ann. Mosell.: Kalendis Iunii); the capitulary is of June 794.

entries.title: Frankfurt: the new deniers must be taken in every place, town and market
entries.effect: coin: the new heavier denier is legal tender everywhere; a free man who refuses it pays 15 solidi
entries.note: The heavy new denier is usually dated 793/794 from this chapter.

entries.title: Frankfurt synod condemns Adoptionism and rejects the Greek council on images
Tassilo, former duke of Bavaria, gives up all his rights at Frankfurt
entries.effect: Bavaria fully royal

entries.title: Cordoban armies raid Alava and Asturias; Alfonso II ambushes one at Lutos
entries.effect: northern Spain at war; Asturian coast unsafe

entries.title: Heathens lay waste all the islands of Britain
entries.effect: routes through the Isles hostile
entries.note: Probably the Hebrides and Western Isles.

entries.title: Heathens plunder the monastery at Donemuthe (Jarrow); a storm wrecks their ships
entries.effect: raid on gyrwe: monastery plundered; raiders' leader killed, storm-wrecked survivors killed on the shore; Tyne mouth dangerous
entries.note: Season not given. Donemuthe is usually Jarrow; Ingram's ASC text reads the mouth of the Wear.

entries.title: Aethelheard, former ealdorman turned cleric, dies at York
Queen Fastrada dies at Frankfurt; buried at St Alban's, Mainz
entries.note: The day only in Ann. Guelf. (4 Id. Aug.).

entries.title: Great drought, yet an abundant harvest
entries.effect: famine ends: grain cheaper from the harvest of 794
entries.note: Ann. Mosell. run a year behind.

entries.title: Two Frankish armies enter Saxony; the Saxons at the Sintfeld submit and give hostages
entries.effect: Saxony briefly quiet; hostages taken into Francia
entries.note: Charles the Younger crossed the Rhine at Cologne.

entries.title: Charles winters at Aachen, from now on his usual winter seat
entries.effect: court at Aachen: steady demand for goods there

entries.title: Bran Ardchenn, king of Leinster, and his queen killed; Finsnechta takes Leinster
entries.effect: Leinster changes hands: a new lord over the Liffey country (duiblinn)
entries.note: AU: the sixth night after the Kalends of May, a Wednesday; 6 May 795 was a Wednesday.

entries.title: Abd al-Karim ibn Mughith sacks Oviedo, the Asturian capital
entries.effect: Asturias ravaged

entries.title: Heathens burn Rechru (Rathlin, or Lambay off Dublin)
entries.effect: North Channel (or the Dublin coast) hostile
entries.note: First Viking raid in the Irish annals. Rathlin (Antrim) and Lambay (Dublin, 53.49,-6.02) are both argued; AFM run about five years early here.

entries.title: Skye overwhelmed and laid waste by heathens (?)
entries.effect: Hebridean waters hostile
entries.note: AU's 'Sci' is read as Skye; another reading makes it the shrines of Rechru.

entries.title: Heathens plunder Iona
entries.effect: raid on hi: monastery plundered; pilgrims and trade at Iona disrupted

entries.title: Heathens plunder Inishmurray and Inishbofin off western Ireland
entries.effect: west-coast islands hostile
entries.note: Inis Bo Finne may be Inishbofin in Galway or in Donegal.

entries.title: Welsh annals note the first coming of the heathens among the southern Irish (?)
entries.note: AC's 'apud dexterales' may mean south Wales or southern Ireland; AC years run a year late here.

entries.title: Offa ravages Rhieinwg in south-west Wales
entries.effect: Mercian army in south Wales
entries.note: AC years run about a year late here (Offa's death under 797).

entries.title: After an assembly at Kostheim, Charles ravages Saxony to the Elbe at Lüne and Bardowick
entries.effect: Lower Elbe under the Frankish army; many hostages
entries.note: Ann. Alam.: 7,070 hostages (one copy 770).

entries.title: Witzin, king of the Abodrites and Frankish ally, killed by Saxons crossing the Elbe
entries.effect: Elbe crossing hostile; Abodrite leadership changes
entries.note: Charles was waiting at Bardowick for his Slav allies (revised ARF).

entries.title: Envoys of the Avar tudun offer his submission and baptism
entries.effect: Avar realm splitting

entries.title: Pope Hadrian I dies; Leo III elected
entries.note: Lorsch and Moissac: VIII Kal. Ian. (25 Dec); Ann. Alam.: 26 Dec; the ARF files it in 796 (its year begins at Christmas).

entries.title: Avar khagan and jugurrus killed by their own people in civil war
entries.effect: Avar realm leaderless; the Ring unguarded

entries.title: Duke Eric of Friuli and the Slav Wonomir plunder the Avar Ring; treasure sent to Aachen
entries.place: the Ring, between Danube and Tisza
entries.effect: centuries of Avar gold, silver and silk flow into Francia
entries.note: Lorsch put the treasure's arrival in 795, the ARF in 796.

entries.title: Eclipse of the moon between cock-crow and dawn
entries.note: v kal. Apr.; HR's year is right, the ASC's a year early.

entries.title: Leo III sends Charles the keys of St Peter's tomb and the banner of Rome
Charles writes to Offa: each realm's merchants protected; pilgrim-traders pay toll
entries.effect: treaty: English merchants protected in the Frankish realm and Frankish ones in Mercia, with appeal to the king; true pilgrims pass free, traders posing as pilgrims pay toll at the usual places; Offa wants the black stones, the Franks English cloaks of the old length
entries.note: Written between Hadrian's death (Dec 795) and Offa's (July 796). It ends a quarrel of about 789/90 that had closed Frankish ports to English traders (Gesta abbatum Fontanellensium).

entries.title: Emir Hisham I of Cordoba dies; his son al-Hakam I succeeds
entries.effect: new emir in al-Andalus; his uncles rise and seek Frankish help
entries.note: Some give 17 April (Safar 180).

entries.title: King Aethelred I of Northumbria killed at Corbridge; Osbald made king
entries.effect: Northumbria in turmoil: lordship and tolls at eoforwic uncertain
entries.note: HR: xiv kal. Mai (18 April); ASC: xiii kal. Mai (19 April), filed under 794.

entries.title: Eardwulf recalled from exile and made king of Northumbria; consecrated at York 26 May
entries.effect: new king at eoforwic
entries.note: ASC: ii id. Mai (14 May) accession, vii kal. Iun. (26 May) consecration, filed under 795; HR gives the 26 May consecration under 796.

entries.title: Osbald deposed after 27 days; sails from Lindisfarne to the king of the Picts
entries.note: 27 days after 18 April is about 15 May.

entries.title: Charles, angered by Aethelred's murder, recalls his gifts and threatens the Northumbrians
entries.effect: Frankish court cool to Northumbria for a time; Northumbrian ships less welcome in Frankish ports (?)
entries.note: Alcuin pleaded for them.

entries.title: Small globes seen around the sun (later English tradition)
Battle of Rhuddlan; Maredudd, king of Dyfed, dies
entries.effect: fighting on the Clwyd near legacaestir: north Welsh coast risky
entries.note: Foes not named; usually taken as Mercian-Welsh fighting. AC years run a year late here.

entries.title: Heathens in Ireland
entries.effect: Irish coasts raided

entries.title: Kardam of Bulgaria demands tribute; Constantine VI waits at Versinikia, no battle
entries.effect: Thrace tense

entries.title: Arab raid reaches Amorion in Anatolia
entries.effect: Anatolian interior unsafe

entries.title: Harun al-Rashid moves his court to al-Raqqa on the Euphrates
entries.effect: caliph's court at Raqqa (to 808); Euphrates and Syrian roads busy

entries.title: Pippin crosses the Danube and destroys the Avar Ring; the new khagan submits
entries.effect: Avar power broken; Danube lands open to Frankish and Bavarian settlers

entries.title: Bishops meet on the Danube to settle how the Avars are to be baptised
entries.effect: mission to the Avars from Salzburg and Aquileia

entries.title: Charles ravages Saxony; the Franks bridge the Weser at Alisni
entries.effect: lower Weser crossing held by the Franks
entries.note: Pertz identified Alisni as Elsfleth (?).

entries.title: A Frankish army raids Saracen lands in Spain
Offa, king of the Mercians, dies; his son Ecgfrith succeeds
entries.effect: Mercian overlordship weakens: Kent and East Anglia break away; lundenwic under a new king
entries.note: ASC: iv kal. Aug. (29 July; Ingram's conflated text also has iv id. Aug.); HR: vii kal. Aug. (26 July). ASC A/E file it two years early under 794.

entries.title: Archbishop Eanbald I of York dies; Eanbald II consecrated at Sockburn on 14 August
entries.effect: new archbishop (and coin-issuer) at eoforwic
entries.note: iv id. Aug.; HR's consecration date is corrected to xix kal. Sept. (14 August), a Sunday.

entries.title: Eadberht Praen seizes Kent; Archbishop Aethelheard flees Canterbury
entries.effect: Kent (sarre, fordwic, dofras) under a rebel king hostile to Mercia
entries.note: Coins in his name were struck at Canterbury. ASC year two early.

entries.title: Eadwald rules East Anglia as an independent king after Offa's death (c. 796-798)
entries.effect: East Anglia briefly free of Mercia
entries.note: Known only from his coins; Cenwulf's coins replace his by about 798.

entries.title: The Avar tudun comes to Aachen with many Avars and is baptised
entries.effect: western Avars become Frankish clients
entries.note: Lorsch and Ann. Alam. put it in 795.

entries.title: Pippin brings the rest of the Avar treasure to Aachen; Charles shares it out
entries.effect: Avar gold and silk reach Rome, Frankish churches and nobles; silver plentiful at court

entries.title: Ecgfrith of Mercia dies after 141 days; Cenwulf king of the Mercians
entries.effect: new Mercian king over lundenwic and legacaestir
entries.note: 141 days after Offa's death is about 14-17 December 796.

entries.title: Zatun, lord of Barcelona, comes to Aachen and hands over his city
entries.effect: Barcelona nominally Frankish (lost again until 801)
entries.note: The first item of ARF 797.

entries.title: Abdallah, exiled uncle of al-Hakam, seeks Charles's help at Aachen
entries.effect: Franks back a rival in al-Andalus; Louis takes him back to Spain

entries.title: Theoktistos, envoy of the governor of Sicily, brings Constantine VI's letter to Aachen
entries.effect: Frankish-Byzantine contacts open

entries.title: Isaac the Jew, Lantfrid and Sigimund sent as envoys to Harun al-Rashid
entries.effect: first Frankish embassy to the Abbasids
entries.note: Year from ARF 801, which says they were sent four years before.

entries.title: Harun campaigns in Asia Minor and takes al-Safsaf; a column raids to Ankara
entries.effect: Anatolia unsafe

entries.title: Mars not seen anywhere in the sky for a whole year
entries.note: From July 797 to July 798.

entries.title: Day of the Ditch: Toledo's notables massacred by al-Hakam's governor (?)
entries.effect: Toledo cowed
entries.note: Sources disagree: 797 (AH 181) or 806/807 (AH 191).

entries.title: King Donnchad of Tara dies; Aed son of Niall wins at Druim Rig and takes the kingship
entries.effect: new Ui Neill over-king

entries.title: Louis sent to besiege Huesca
entries.note: Ann. Alam.: Louis came back without a battle.

entries.title: Charles marches through the marshes to Hadeln on the sea; Wigmodia taken
entries.effect: Elbe-Weser coast occupied; Saxons and Frisians give hostages

entries.title: Royal ships hauled overland and by river into Saxony; camp fortified with them
entries.effect: royal river fleet on Saxon rivers

entries.title: Constantine VI blinded in the Porphyra; Irene rules alone
entries.effect: Irene sole ruler; the Franks treat the imperial throne as vacant
entries.note: Theophanes writes 'Saturday 15 August', but the 15th was a Tuesday; 19 August 797 was the Saturday.

entries.title: Sun darkened for seventeen days after the blinding; ships lose their way
entries.effect: dim sun: ships go astray (portent)

entries.title: Archbishop Eanbald II of York receives the pallium
entries.note: vi id. Sept. (8 Sept), the Nativity of Mary, in the ASC; HR's 'iv id.' is a slip, as its own feast-day shows.

entries.title: Capitulare Saxonicum issued at Aachen with Saxons from all parts
entries.effect: law: Saxon fines and peace terms set, milder than the 782 regime

entries.title: Charles winters in Saxony at Herstelle on the Weser; army billeted across Saxony
entries.effect: army quartered in Saxony all winter: food requisitioned
entries.note: Entered Saxony mid-November.

entries.title: At Herstelle: Avar envoys with rich gifts and an envoy of Alfonso II of Asturias
entries.note: Alfonso's envoy Froia brought a fine tent.

entries.title: Alfonso II sacks Lisbon; sends Charles mail-coats, mules and Moorish captives
entries.effect: Atlantic coast of al-Andalus raided; Lisbon disrupted

entries.title: Rebels under Wada beaten by King Eardwulf near Whalley; Alric son of Heardberht slain
entries.effect: Eardwulf secures Northumbria
entries.note: ASC: iv non. Apr. (2 April), in Lent (Easter 8 April). HR: at Billingahoth near Walalege.

entries.title: Saxons beyond the Elbe kill royal envoys, among them Godescalc back from the Danish king
entries.effect: north bank of the Elbe hostile; road to the Danes cut
entries.note: At Easter time (8 April 798). Revised ARF: the army could not leave winter quarters for lack of fodder. Sigfrid's last mention.

entries.title: Irene's envoys Michael and Theophilus seek peace at Aachen; Sisinnius released
entries.effect: Frankish-Byzantine peace talks

entries.title: Moors and Saracens plunder the Balearic Islands
entries.effect: western Mediterranean shipping unsafe

entries.title: Arabs raid to Malagina and seize the imperial horses; Irene buys a truce
entries.effect: Byzantium pays the Caliphate tribute

entries.title: London destroyed by an accidental fire with great loss of life
entries.effect: fire at lundenwic: quays and stores burned; goods scarce and dear

entries.title: Cenwulf ravages Kent, captures Eadberht Praen and maims him; Cuthred made king
entries.effect: Kent laid waste by the Mercian army, then ruled by Cuthred, Cenwulf's brother
entries.note: ASC year two early (Ingram's text has it under 796).

entries.title: Leo III refuses to move the southern archbishopric to London; condemns Eadberht
sources: Leo III to Cenwulf, 798 (Haddan & Stubbs III)
entries.effect: Canterbury stays the seat of the southern church

entries.title: Synod at Pincanhalh (Finchale) under Eanbald II on Easter and church law
Heathens burn Inis Patraic, take the cattle-tribute and break the shrine of Do-Chonna
entries.effect: raid on the Brega coast north of duiblinn: cattle and church treasure carried off
entries.note: AU adds great incursions in Ireland and Alba.

entries.title: Caradog, king of Gwynedd, killed by the Saxons
entries.effect: Gwynedd leaderless; Mercian pressure on north Wales

entries.title: From Minden Charles ravages Saxony between Weser and Elbe; 1,600 hostages deported
entries.effect: Saxon heartland burned; leading Saxons spread through Francia

entries.title: Abodrites under Thrasco crush the Nordalbingians at Bornhöved (Suentana)
entries.effect: Abodrites masters between Elbe and Eider; Frankish-Abodrite alliance
entries.note: ARF: 4,000 Saxons killed; Lorsch: 2,901; Moissac: 2,800.

entries.title: Great snowfall in Ireland kills many people and cattle
entries.effect: harsh winter in Ireland: cattle lost; hides and butter scarce, food dear

entries.title: Irene rides in a gold chariot through Constantinople on Easter Monday, scattering coin
entries.effect: coin given out in the capital
entries.note: Easter 799 was 31 March.

entries.title: Pope Leo III attacked in Rome during the Greater Litany procession
Daniel, envoy of Michael, governor of Sicily, received by Charles in Saxony
entries.effect: Byzantine Sicily in touch with the Franks

entries.title: A monk from Jerusalem brings relics of the Holy Sepulchre from the patriarch
Saxons deported with wives and children; their land shared among Frankish lords
entries.effect: Saxon land resettled by Franks

entries.title: A great church built and dedicated at Paderborn
The Avars break faith and rise against Frankish rule
entries.effect: Danube frontier at war

entries.title: Duke Eric of Friuli killed in an ambush by the townsmen of Tarsatica
entries.effect: head of the Kvarner Gulf hostile to the Franks

entries.title: The Balearics submit to the Franks after help against raiders; Moorish banners sent
entries.effect: Balearics under Frankish protection

entries.title: Count Wido of the Breton march tours Brittany and takes its submission
entries.effect: Brittany submits (briefly): the coast west of Nantes quieter

entries.title: Azan, governor of Huesca, sends Charles the keys of his city
entries.effect: Ebro frontier lords courting the Franks

entries.title: Pagan ships raid islands off Aquitaine; about 105 raiders killed on the shore
entries.effect: Bay of Biscay islands (the salt island of Herio) unsafe
entries.note: Islands not named: Noirmoutier or Re (?). The letter to Arn is usually dated 799.

entries.title: Khazars break through Derbent into Armenia and carry off many captives
entries.effect: Caucasus route closed; Khazar-Caliphate war

entries.title: Plot of Akameros, lord of the Slavs of Belzetia, for the sons of Constantine V crushed
entries.effect: Slav districts of Greece restless

entries.title: Many ships wrecked with their crews by a violent storm in the British sea
entries.effect: storm: heavy losses of ships; sailing risk high this year
entries.note: Where exactly is not said.

entries.title: Duke Moll killed on King Eardwulf's orders
Osbald, once king, later abbot, dies and is buried at York
Duke Aldred, slayer of King Aethelred, killed by Torhtmund in revenge
Brorda (Hildegils), a leading Mercian ealdorman, dies
Sigeric, king of the East Saxons, leaves his kingdom for Rome
entries.note: The same annal holds the Rome journey of 801, so this may belong to 799-801 (?).

entries.title: Bishop Aelfhun of Dommoc dies at Sudbury and is buried at Dunwich
entries.effect: new bishop at dommoc
entries.note: Year uncertain within 797-801.

entries.title: Law of Patrick proclaimed in Connacht by Gormgal son of Dindathach
entries.effect: law: Cain Patraic in Connacht

entries.title: Assembly at Lippeham; Charles camps at Paderborn and receives Pope Leo there
entries.effect: court and army at Paderborn
entries.note: Leo was escorted back to Rome and restored.

entries.title: Charles the Younger meets the Slavs and the Nordalbingians in the Bardengau
entries.effect: Elbe frontier settled for the season

entries.title: Gerold, prefect of Bavaria, falls fighting the Avars
entries.effect: Bavarian march leaderless
entries.note: ARF gives the year only; 1 September from his commemoration.

entries.title: Thunder and lightning on St Michael's Day, called fire from heaven
Eclipse of the moon in the evening
entries.note: xvii kal. Feb.; this fits 16 January 800 itself, though the same annal's death of Beorhtric belongs to 802.

entries.title: Charles inspects the Channel coast, sets up a fleet and posts guards against pirates
entries.effect: coastguard posts and a royal fleet on the Channel coast against pirates
entries.note: Left Aachen mid-March; Easter (19 Apr) at Saint-Riquier, then Rouen and over the Seine to Tours. The revised ARF calls the pirates Northmen.

entries.title: Queen Liutgard dies at Tours
entries.note: Moissac: a great assembly at Tours where Charles arranged the realm for his sons.

entries.title: Harun makes Ibrahim ibn al-Aghlab hereditary emir of Ifriqiya
entries.effect: Aghlabid Ifriqiya: a new sea power facing Sicily and Sardinia

entries.title: Alhmund, son of King Alhred, seized and killed by King Eardwulf's guards
entries.note: Later venerated as a saint at Derby.

entries.title: Heathens plunder the churches of Hartness and Tynemouth (?)
entries.effect: Tyne and Tees coast hostile
entries.note: Only in Wendover; perhaps from lost northern annals, perhaps a later elaboration.

entries.title: Unusual hard frost in July (again on 9 July), with no harm to the crops
entries.effect: none on the harvest
entries.note: pridie Non. Iul. and VII Id. Iul.

entries.title: Assembly at Mainz; Charles sets out for Italy
Pippin sent to ravage the duchy of Benevento
Charles enters Rome, met by Leo at Mentana the day before
entries.note: Assembly on 1 December.

entries.title: Leo III clears himself by oath; envoys bring the keys of the Holy Sepulchre
entries.effect: Frankish link to Jerusalem; pilgrims and alms flow east
entries.note: The ARF puts both on the same day without a date; 23 December from the Liber Pontificalis.

entries.title: Christmas Eve gale throws down towns and houses; the sea floods the land; many cattle die
entries.effect: storm surge: coastal flooding, buildings down, cattle lost; North Sea harbours damaged
entries.note: HR: ix kal. Ian., wind from the south-west or west; Wendover: 23 December, a south wind.

entries.title: Leo III crowns Charles emperor of the Romans in St Peter's
entries.effect: Charles now emperor and augustus
entries.note: The ARF files it under 801 (its year begins at Christmas).

entries.title: Leo's attackers condemned for treason; spared and exiled at the pope's plea
Pestilence after a mild winter
entries.effect: sickness: fewer hands

entries.title: Irene remits Constantinople's city taxes and the customs of Abydos and Hieron
entries.effect: law: straits customs cut; cheaper passage for ships to and from Constantinople

entries.title: Charles leaves Rome after Easter; Pippin's second Benevento campaign
entries.note: VII Kal. Mai.

entries.title: Great earthquake shakes Italy; the roof of St Paul's in Rome falls in
entries.effect: Italian towns damaged
entries.note: II Kal. Mai., at the second hour of the night.

entries.title: Earth tremors around the Rhine, in Gaul and in Germany
Envoys of Harun and of Ibrahim of Kairouan land at Pisa; Charles meets them near Vercelli
entries.effect: news that Isaac is coming back with great gifts
entries.note: Lantfrid and Sigimund had died on the way. Charles kept St John's day (24 June) at Ivrea.

entries.title: Eardwulf of Northumbria makes war on Cenwulf of Mercia; peace sworn on the Gospels
entries.effect: Humber frontier hostile for a season, then peace
entries.note: Cenwulf had sheltered Eardwulf's enemies; the bishops and leading men of both sides made the peace.

entries.title: Bishop Heathoberht of London dies; soon after a great part of London burns
entries.effect: fire at lundenwic: quays and stores burned; prices up

entries.title: Archbishop Aethelheard and Bishop Cyneberht go to Rome over Canterbury's rights
entries.note: ASC year two early; it led to Leo III's privilege of January 802.

entries.title: Bresal son of Segene, abbot of Iona for 31 years, dies
entries.effect: new abbot at hi

entries.title: Notary Ercanbald sent to Liguria to fit out ships for the elephant
Barcelona falls to the Franks after a long siege; Zatun captured
entries.effect: Barcelona Frankish: a Christian port on the Spanish March
entries.note: ARF: a two-year siege; Moissac (under 803): seven months, Louis entering at the end.

entries.title: Chieti taken and burned; its forts surrender
A rainy summer in Ireland
entries.effect: wet harvest: grain dear in Ireland

entries.title: Isaac lands at Porto Venere with the elephant; Alpine snow keeps him at Vercelli
entries.effect: Alpine passes closed by snow from October

entries.title: Leo III confirms Canterbury's authority over all the southern sees
sources: Leo III to Aethelheard, 18 Jan 802 (Haddan & Stubbs III)
entries.effect: prepares the end of the Lichfield archbishopric

entries.title: Irene's envoy Leo at Aachen; Bishop Jesse and Count Helmgaud sent to Constantinople
entries.effect: Frankish-Byzantine talks; Theophanes reports a marriage proposal

entries.title: Capitulare missorum generale: all free men over 12 swear fidelity to the emperor
entries.effect: missi (bishops, abbots, counts) tour the realm to do justice

entries.title: Missi told to have ships readied on the sea coasts and coast-dwellers ready to muster
entries.effect: coastal defence: ships on the Channel coast; free men near the sea called out on a messenger's word
entries.note: In the capitularies for the missi of the Orleans, Paris and Rouen districts.

entries.title: Charles sends a second embassy (Radbert) to Harun al-Rashid
entries.note: Year from ARF 806, which says the envoys were sent four years before.

entries.title: Ortona and Lucera surrender; Grimoald later captures Count Winigis at Lucera
entries.note: Winigis was sent back in 803.

entries.title: Patriarch John of Grado killed on the orders of the Venetian doge's son
sources: John the Deacon, Istoria Veneticorum II
entries.effect: Venetian lagoon split; the new patriarch turns to the Franks
entries.note: Chronicle of about 1000; date approximate.

entries.title: Counts Cadaloh and Goteram killed by Avars near the castle of Guntio
entries.effect: Pannonian march still fighting
entries.note: The exact annal is not verified.

entries.title: Beorhtric of Wessex dies, said to be poisoned; Ecgberht back from exile as king
entries.effect: new king of Wessex: hamwic under Ecgberht
entries.note: ASC year two early. Ecgberht had been in exile in Francia.

entries.title: Battle at Kempsford: ealdormen Aethelmund and Weohstan both killed; Wiltshire wins
entries.effect: Mercian-West Saxon border war on the upper Thames
entries.note: Fought on the day Ecgberht became king.

entries.title: Beorhtric's widow Eadburh flees with treasure to Charles, who gives her a nunnery
entries.note: Later expelled; said to have died a beggar at Pavia.

entries.title: Iona burned by heathens
entries.effect: raid on hi: monastery burned

entries.title: A Saxon army ravages the Saxons beyond the Elbe
The elephant Abul Abaz reaches Aachen with Harun's gifts
entries.effect: eastern luxury gifts at court
entries.note: XIII Kal. Aug.

entries.title: Aachen synod and assembly: canons, the Rule and the peoples' laws read and written
entries.effect: law: each people's law written down; judges to judge by written law and take no gifts

entries.title: Nikephoros, minister of finance, deposes Irene and is crowned emperor
entries.effect: new emperor; Irene's tax remissions to be reversed; Frankish envoys present

entries.title: Harun's pilgrimage: the succession pact for al-Amin and al-Ma'mun hung in the Kaaba
entries.effect: Caliphate divided in advance: Iraq to al-Amin, Khurasan to al-Ma'mun
entries.note: Dhu al-Hijja 186 is about December 802.

entries.title: Eclipse of the moon at dawn (date doubtful)
entries.note: xiii kal. Ian.; no lunar eclipse fits 20 December in these years, so the entry may be misdated.

entries.title: Earthquake around Aachen and nearby lands, followed by a mortality
entries.effect: sickness around Aachen

entries.title: Ja'far the Barmakid executed; the Barmakid ministers fall
entries.effect: Caliphate's chief ministers gone; their wealth seized
entries.note: Night of 1 Safar 187 (28/29 January 803).

entries.title: Nikephoros stops Irene's tribute; Harun's son al-Qasim raids Byzantine Anatolia
entries.effect: Arab-Byzantine war again

entries.title: Higbald, bishop of Lindisfarne, dies; Ecgberht consecrated at Bywell on 11 June
entries.effect: new bishop at lindisfarena
entries.note: Symeon: viii kal. Iun. (25 May); the ASC: 24 June. Consecration iii id. Iun. (11 June 803), Trinity Sunday.

entries.title: Assembly at Mainz; no campaign this year
entries.effect: a peaceful year

entries.title: Capitulary for the missi: no arm-rings or byrnies to merchants; measures to be equal
entries.effect: law: arms trade restricted; standard measures enforced

entries.title: Skiringssal (Kaupang): earliest tree-ring date, a jetty timber felled in 803
entries.effect: the market at Skiringssal being built about 800
entries.note: Archaeological date, not a recorded event.

entries.title: Nikephoros's envoys meet Charles at Salz and take home a written peace draft
entries.effect: Frankish-Byzantine peace draft (Venice and Dalmatia at stake)
entries.note: The Frankish envoys had reached Constantinople just before Irene fell.

entries.title: Bardanes Tourkos proclaimed emperor by the Anatolian army; the revolt soon collapses
entries.effect: brief civil war in Anatolia

entries.title: Irene dies in exile on Lesbos
Council of Clofesho abolishes the Lichfield archbishopric; Canterbury's province restored
sources: Acts of the Council of Clofesho, 12 Oct 803 (Birch 310, 312)
entries.effect: one archbishop for the south (Canterbury); laymen not to rule minsters

entries.title: In Bavaria Charles settles Pannonian affairs; Avar and Slav leaders submit
entries.effect: Danube trade via Regensburg reopens
entries.note: Back at Aachen in December.

entries.title: Storm on St Patrick's Eve kills 1,010 in Corcu Baiscinn; the sea splits the island of Fita
entries.effect: storm surge on the Clare coast: Shannon mouth dangerous; farmland buried in sand
entries.note: The night before 17 March. Fita is thought to be Mutton Island.

entries.title: Alcuin, abbot of St Martin's at Tours, dies
entries.note: Whitsunday, at dawn.

entries.title: Synod of the Ui Neill at Dun Cuair; clergy freed from going on hostings
entries.effect: law: clerics exempt from hostings in Ui Neill lands

entries.title: Aed son of Niall ravages Leinster twice in a month; King Finsnechta submits
entries.effect: war in Leinster: the Liffey country (duiblinn) plundered

entries.title: Kells (Cenannas) given to the community of Colum Cille
entries.effect: the Iona community gains a safe inland house

entries.title: Lyminge nuns given a plot inside Canterbury as a refuge
entries.effect: the Kentish coast felt unsafe (?)
entries.note: Often read as a response to coastal raiding; the charter does not name the danger.

entries.title: Saxons of Wigmodia and beyond the Elbe deported; Nordalbingia given to the Abodrites
entries.effect: Elbe-Weser lands emptied; Abodrites hold the land up to the Danish border; the Saxon war ends
entries.note: Einhard: 10,000 people from both banks of the Elbe spread through Gaul and Germany.

entries.title: Godfred of the Danes brings his fleet and all his horse to Sliesthorp
entries.effect: Danish fleet massed at the Schlei; border tense
entries.note: Sliesthorp first named. Godfred stayed away from the meeting; envoys were sent about fugitives.

entries.title: Charles camps at Hollenstedt; the Abodrite prince Thrasco brings gifts
entries.note: Charles was at Cologne by mid-September.

entries.title: Nikephoros beaten by the Arabs at Krasos in Phrygia, barely escaping
entries.effect: Anatolia raided

entries.title: Pope Leo III visits Charles: met at Reims, Christmas at Quierzy, then Aachen
entries.note: He stayed eight days and went home through Bavaria to Ravenna.

entries.title: Prisoner exchange on the Lamos in Cilicia: about 3,700 Muslim captives freed
entries.effect: truce on the Cilician frontier

entries.title: Avar capcan Theodore given land between Sabaria and Carnuntum; khagan restored
entries.effect: Avars under Frankish protection, pressed by the Slavs

entries.title: Archbishop Aethelheard of Canterbury dies; Wulfred chosen to succeed
entries.note: ASC year two early; 12 May from Canterbury obits.

entries.title: Avar khagan baptised as Abraham at the river Fischa
entries.note: Often dated 21 September 805; the day is not verified.

entries.title: Aed son of Niall divides Leinster between two Muiredachs at Dun Cuair
entries.effect: Leinster split: duiblinn's overlord changes

entries.title: Peterhof hoard: youngest dirham about 804/5, Abbasid silver at the Gulf of Finland
entries.effect: silver moving north by the Volga to the Baltic
entries.note: Coin evidence, buried some time after its youngest coin; the t.p.q. is not verified.

entries.title: Peloponnesian Slavs, with Saracen ships, besiege Patras and fail (?)
entries.effect: Gulf of Patras unsafe
entries.note: Dated only to Nikephoros I's reign; 805 and 807 both proposed.

entries.title: Plot of Cordoban notables against al-Hakam crushed; 72 executed (?)
entries.effect: Cordoba tense

entries.title: Krum destroys what is left of the eastern Avar khaganate (?)
entries.note: Late source, no year; about 803-805 is a modern estimate.

entries.title: Charles the Younger ravages Bohemia; Duke Lecho killed
entries.effect: Bohemia hostile
entries.note: He rejoined his father at Camp in the Vosges.

entries.title: A Frankish force sails up the Elbe to Magdeburg and ravages Genewara
entries.effect: royal ships on the Elbe as far as Magdeburg

entries.title: Famine in many parts of the realm
entries.effect: grain dear across Francia 805-807; relief ordered

entries.title: Thionville: trade with Slavs and Avars only at named border posts; no arms sold
entries.effect: law: merchants going to the Slavs and Avars stop at Bardowick, Schezla, Magdeburg, Erfurt, Hallstadt, Forchheim, Premberg, Regensburg and Lorch, each under a royal missus; arms or byrnies found = all their goods seized
entries.note: Issued at the winter court of 805/806. Breemberga is Premberg on the Naab (one list read Pfreimd).

entries.title: Thionville: in this famine each must feed his own; no dear grain, no food sold abroad
entries.effect: famine law: no food sold outside the empire; grain not to be sold too dear

entries.title: Thionville: only old, just tolls on bridges, ships and markets; new tolls banned
entries.effect: tolls: none for passing under bridges or for goods moved without trade

entries.title: Thionville: coin to be struck only at the palace; good deniers in use stay valid
entries.effect: coin: local mints shut because of false coin

entries.title: Thionville: a byrnie for every 12 manses; no arms carried at home; feuds to be settled
entries.effect: demand for byrnies inside the realm; feuds curbed

entries.title: Doges of Venice and envoys of Zadar submit to Charles at Thionville
entries.effect: Venice and Dalmatia on the Frankish side; Byzantium will answer by sea
entries.note: Just after Christmas 805.

entries.title: Divisio regnorum at Thionville: the realm split among Charles, Pippin and Louis
entries.effect: merchants' goods (gold, silver, gems, arms, cloth, slaves) may cross the three kingdoms, land may not; Venice, Istria and Dalmatia go to Pippin's Italy
entries.note: Leo III signed it (taken to him by Einhard).

entries.title: Charles sails down Moselle and Rhine to Nijmegen; Lent and Easter there
entries.effect: court at Nijmegen: demand for goods in the Rhine delta
entries.note: Easter 12 April 806.

entries.title: Nijmegen capitulary: famine price caps; buying grain at harvest to sell dear banned
entries.effect: law: most per modius oats 2 d., barley 3, spelt 3, rye 4, wheat 6; hoarding is 'turpe lucrum'; lords feed their own

entries.title: Nijmegen capitulary: church treasure not to be sold off to Jewish and other merchants
entries.effect: merchants may not buy church plate

entries.title: A cross seen in the moon at dawn
entries.note: ii non. Iun.; the ASC says a Wednesday, but 4 June 806 was a Thursday (perhaps the dawn after Wednesday night).

entries.title: Harun's great army leaves Raqqa to invade Byzantine Cappadocia
entries.effect: full Arab invasion of Anatolia
entries.note: Tabari gives 135,000 men.

entries.title: Count William of Toulouse becomes a monk at Gellone
entries.note: Feast of Sts Peter and Paul.

entries.title: Moors ravage Corsica; Pippin's fleet sent; Count Hadumar of Genoa killed
entries.effect: Corsican waters hostile; Genoa leaderless

entries.title: Moors seize sixty monks on Pantelleria and sell them as slaves in Spain
entries.effect: slave raids in the Sicilian channel; captives sold in al-Andalus
entries.note: ARF 807 says 'the year before'; some were later ransomed by Charles.

entries.title: Navarrese and Pamplonans return to Frankish allegiance
entries.effect: western Pyrenees passes Frankish again

entries.title: Nikephoros sends a fleet under the patrician Niketas to recover Dalmatia
entries.effect: Byzantine fleet in the Adriatic; Venice and Dalmatia contested

entries.title: Charles's envoys back from Harun slip past the Greek fleet into the port of Treviso
entries.effect: Adriatic patrolled by Byzantium

entries.title: Arab fleet under Humayd raids Cyprus and carries off some 16,000 captives
entries.effect: eastern Mediterranean shipping unsafe

entries.title: Rafi ibn al-Layth rebels at Samarqand against Abbasid rule
entries.effect: eastern silver routes unsettled

entries.title: Great pestilence breaks out in Ireland
entries.effect: sickness in Ireland: fewer buyers and crews

entries.title: Heathens kill sixty-eight of the community of Iona
entries.effect: raid on hi: community slaughtered; the monks look to Kells

entries.title: Law of Patrick proclaimed by Aed son of Niall
entries.effect: law: Cain Patraic in Ui Neill lands

entries.title: Finsnechta son of Cellach takes back the kingship of Leinster
King Eardwulf driven out of Northumbria; Aelfwald II takes the kingdom
entries.effect: Northumbria under a rival king
entries.note: ASC D/E date the expulsion 806; Wendover puts it in 808 and gives Aelfwald two years.

entries.title: Archbishop Wulfred of Canterbury receives the pallium
Charles the Younger beats the Sorbs; Miliduoch killed; forts on the Saale and Elbe
entries.effect: Saale-Elbe frontier fortified (Halle; opposite Magdeburg)

entries.title: An army from Bavaria, Alemannia and Burgundy ravages Bohemia again
entries.effect: Bohemia hostile

entries.title: Harun takes Herakleia after a month's siege; Nikephoros agrees to pay yearly tribute
entries.effect: Byzantium pays tribute (30,000 nomismata in Theophanes, 50,000 in Tabari) and a head tax

entries.title: A great ring seen around the sun
entries.note: iii kal. Sept.

entries.title: Eclipse of the moon
entries.note: ASC: 1 September; ARF: IIII Non. Sept. (2 September) - the night of 1/2 September.

entries.title: Great crop of mast (acorns and nuts) in Ireland
entries.effect: pigs fattened cheaply: pork and lard plentiful
entries.note: Season inferred.

entries.title: Jupiter seen passing across the moon
entries.note: pridie Kal. Febr.

entries.title: Eclipse of the sun at midday
entries.note: III Id. Febr.; AC gives the year only.

entries.title: Eclipse of the moon; great battle-lines (an aurora?) seen in the sky that night
entries.note: IIII Kal. Mart.

entries.title: A small black spot, taken for Mercury, seen on the sun for eight days
entries.note: XVI Kal. Apr.; in fact a sunspot.

entries.title: Famine: only men west of the Seine called up; poorer men club together to equip one
entries.effect: famine eases the call-up; army to be at the Rhine by mid-August

entries.title: Harun's envoy and Jerusalem monks bring a tent, silks, balsam and a brass water clock
who: George of the Mount of Olives
entries.effect: eastern luxuries at court: silk, perfumes, balsam, brass; the envoys wait in Italy for the sailing season
entries.note: The Frankish envoy Radbert died on the way home.

entries.title: Moors lose 3,000 men in Sardinia; Burchard's fleet beats them off Corsica, taking 13 ships
entries.effect: Tyrrhenian raiders checked for the season

entries.title: Niketas, with the Byzantine fleet at Venice, makes a truce with Pippin until August
sources: John the Deacon, Istoria Veneticorum II
entries.effect: truce in the Adriatic until August 807; Venice back under Byzantine sway

entries.title: Nikephoros's march on Bulgaria turned back at Adrianople by a plot
entries.effect: Thracian frontier unsettled

entries.title: The moon turns the colour of blood
entries.note: A lunar eclipse: 26 February or 22 August 807.

entries.title: Heathens burn Inishmurray and attack Ros Comain
entries.effect: Sligo and Galway Bay coasts hostile
entries.note: AU reads Ros Comain (inland Roscommon); CS reads Ros Cam on Galway Bay, likelier for a sea raid.

entries.title: New monastery of Colum Cille built at Kells
entries.effect: Iona community's centre shifts toward Kells

entries.title: Conall son of Tadc killed by Conall son of Aedan in Kintyre
entries.effect: struggle for the kingship of Dal Riata

entries.title: Cuthred, king of Kent under Mercia, dies; Cenwulf rules Kent directly
entries.effect: Kentish ports under Cenwulf of Mercia
entries.note: Wendover's successor Baldred belongs to about 823.

entries.title: Arthen, king of Ceredigion, dies
Assembly at Ingelheim; no campaign this year
entries.effect: a peaceful year

entries.title: Eclipse of the moon at the third hour of the night
entries.note: XI Kal. Sept.

entries.title: Humayd's Arab fleet sacks Rhodes; a storm wrecks ships off Myra
entries.effect: Aegean raided; storms on the Lycian coast
entries.note: The Theophanes year is uncertain.

entries.title: Charles orders three three-day fasts against barren land, famine and pestilence
sources: MGH Capit. I no. 124 (letter to Ghaerbald)
entries.effect: poor harvests and famine feared; war with pagans on the marches

entries.title: A very mild and pestilent winter
entries.effect: sickness; stores keep badly

entries.title: Exiled King Eardwulf of Northumbria comes to Charles at Nijmegen, then goes to Rome
entries.note: In Lent 808 (2 March-15 April).

entries.title: Capitulary caps cloak and fur prices; only palace deniers to pass
entries.effect: law: best double cloak 20 solidi, single 10; marten or otter coat 30; fine 40 solidi; coin only from the palace

entries.title: Agenda of 808: guard the march by land and sea; the ships ordered to be built
entries.effect: coastal defence and shipbuilding

entries.title: Second prisoner exchange on the Lamos; new Arab-Byzantine truce
entries.effect: truce on the Cilician frontier

entries.title: Harun sets out for Khurasan to put down Rafi's revolt
entries.effect: the caliph leaves Raqqa; court moves east

entries.title: Finsnechta son of Cellach, king of Leinster, dies at Kildare
The men of Leinster defeat Aed son of Niall at the Liffey
entries.effect: fighting on the Liffey near duiblinn

entries.title: Rhain, king of Dyfed, and Cadell, king of Powys, die
Godfred attacks the Abodrites; two thirds made tributary; his nephew Reginold killed
entries.effect: Abodrite lands under Danish tribute; the Wilzi side with the Danes
entries.note: Thrasco driven out; Godelaib hanged.

entries.title: Charles the Younger bridges the Elbe and ravages the Linones and Smeldingi
entries.effect: middle Elbe hostile

entries.title: Godfred destroys the emporium of Reric and moves its merchants to Sliesthorp
entries.effect: port closed: Reric wrecked; its merchants and the king's tolls move to Sliesthorp (Hedeby)
entries.note: ARF: called Reric in the Danes' tongue; it paid the Danish king large tolls.

entries.title: Godfred orders a rampart along the Eider from the Baltic to the North Sea, with one gate
entries.effect: Danish border walled: one gate for carts and riders
entries.note: No Danevirke phase is yet tied securely to 808 (the earliest timbers are of 737-c. 740).

entries.title: Two Frankish forts built on the Elbe against Slav raids
entries.effect: Elbe crossings garrisoned

entries.title: Eardwulf brought back to Northumbria by papal and imperial envoys
entries.effect: Eardwulf restored at eoforwic (for how long is unknown)
entries.note: Envoys: the deacon Aldulf for the pope, abbots Hruotfrid and Nanthar for the emperor.

entries.title: Bulgars fall on the army at the Strymon and seize its pay of 1,100 pounds of gold
entries.effect: Strymon valley unsafe
entries.note: AM 6301 = Sept 808-Aug 809; some date it 807.

entries.title: Byzantine fleet winters at Venice; its attack on Comacchio is beaten off
entries.effect: Po delta trade (Comacchio salt) disrupted; Adriatic at war

entries.title: Harun al-Rashid dies at Tus; al-Amin caliph in Baghdad, al-Ma'mun holds Khurasan
entries.effect: new caliph; rivalry between the brothers

entries.title: Liudger, bishop of Münster and missionary to Frisia, dies at Billerbeck
Krum takes Serdica and kills its garrison of 6,000
entries.effect: Balkan land road closed
entries.note: Before Easter (8 April 809).

entries.title: Moors from Spain sack a Corsican town on Holy Saturday
entries.effect: Corsican town emptied; captives to al-Andalus
entries.note: Easter 809 was 8 April. Only the bishop and a few old and sick were left.

entries.title: Greek raiders (Orobiotae) plunder Populonia on the Tuscan coast
entries.effect: Tuscan coast raided

entries.title: Louis besieges Tortosa on the Ebro and withdraws
entries.effect: Ebro mouth contested

entries.title: Count Aureolus of the Pyrenean march dies; Amoroz of Zaragoza seizes his forts
entries.effect: Pyrenean march changes hands
entries.note: Amoroz offered submission; the parley failed in 810.

entries.title: Godfred sends word by merchants; talks at Badenfliot end without result
entries.effect: merchants as go-betweens; border talks fail
entries.note: The place is named only in the revised text.

entries.title: Thrasco ravages the Wilzi and storms the chief fort of the Smeldingi
entries.effect: Abodrite power restored for a time
entries.note: Moissac names the place Connoburg.

entries.title: Papal envoy Aldulf seized by pirates crossing to the continent; ransomed in Britain
entries.effect: Channel crossings unsafe: pirates take passengers for ransom
entries.note: On the envoys' way back from restoring Eardwulf; the others crossed safely. One of Cenwulf's men ransomed him.

entries.title: Capitularies of 809: Sunday markets only where old; no toll where no bridge or ferry helps
entries.effect: law: no new Sunday markets; no forced bridge tolls; good deniers must be taken; no buying crops before harvest

entries.title: Great cattle plague comes from the east and spreads west
entries.effect: murrain: oxen and cattle die; draught animals scarce

entries.title: Aed son of Niall invades Ulaid after Patrick's shrine at Tullylish is violated
entries.effect: east Ulster coast disturbed

entries.title: Ecgberht of Wessex attacks Cornwall (?)
entries.effect: Dumnonian coast at war (?)
entries.note: The ASC puts Ecgberht's Cornish ravaging under 813 (=815), so this may be misdated.

entries.title: Eclipse of the sun in late morning
entries.note: xvii kal. Aug., at the fifth hour; it fits 16 July 809, two years after the ASC's year.

entries.title: Nikephoros orders settlers from the themes moved into the Slav lands of Greece
entries.effect: Greek interior resettled and taxed
entries.note: Begun in September, finished by Easter 810.

entries.title: Council at Aachen on the filioque and church discipline
entries.note: Bernharius of Worms and Adalhard of Corbie sent to Rome.

entries.title: Abodrite prince Thrasco murdered at the emporium of Reric by Godfred's men
entries.effect: Abodrites leaderless; Reric still a trading place in 809
entries.note: The ARF tells it while men were being gathered for a fort beyond the Elbe (late 809); Moissac under 810.

entries.title: Eclipse of the moon
entries.note: VII Kal. Ian.

entries.title: Flood greater than any seen before; the waters highest on 28 December
entries.effect: Scarpe and Scheldt valleys flooded; roads and fields under water
entries.note: If the annal begins its year at Christmas this is 28 December 808 (?).

entries.title: Count Egbert occupies Esesfeld on the Stör and begins to fortify it
entries.effect: Frankish stronghold north of the Elbe; the road to Hedeby watched
entries.note: ARF: about the Ides of March, told within the 809 entry after the November council, so March 810.

entries.title: Pippin attacks Venice by land and sea and takes its submission; his fleet raids Dalmatia
sources: John the Deacon, Istoria Veneticorum II
entries.effect: war in the lagoon; the Frankish fleet withdraws when Paul's Byzantine fleet comes
entries.note: Venetian tradition moves the ducal seat to Rialto after this siege.

entries.title: A great Moorish fleet from Spain strikes Sardinia, then takes almost all Corsica
entries.effect: Corsica held by raiders; Tyrrhenian routes hostile

entries.title: Rotrud, the emperor's eldest daughter, dies
entries.note: VII Id. Iun. (7 June) in Kurze's text; some copies VIII Id. (6 June).

entries.title: Eclipse of the sun
entries.note: VII Id. Iun.; Ann. Xant.: VI Id. Iun. (8 June).

entries.title: Danish fleet of 200 ships ravages the Frisian islands; Frisians pay 100 pounds of silver
entries.effect: raid: Frisian islands sacked, three battles lost, 100 pounds of silver paid; Frisian coastal trade disrupted
entries.note: The news reached Charles at Aachen between 7 June and 8 July; Godfred himself stayed home.

entries.title: Eclipse of the moon
entries.note: XI Kal. Iul.

entries.title: Charles musters at Lippeham; the elephant Abul Abaz dies there
Nikephoros's 'vexations': forced loans to shipowners; tax on slaves bought beyond Abydos
entries.effect: law: the capital's shipowners must borrow 12 pounds of gold at about 16.7%; private loans at interest banned; slaves bought west of Abydos taxed 2 nomismata

entries.title: Charles camps at the Aller-Weser confluence (Verden) awaiting Godfred
entries.note: Ann. S. Amandi: Wends came to him there and he gave them a king.

entries.title: Cattle plague throughout Britain
entries.effect: murrain in Britain: cattle, hides and dairy scarce; meat dear

entries.title: Mynyw (St Davids) burned
entries.note: Cause not stated.

entries.title: The moon darkened (Welsh annals)
entries.note: Probably one of the lunar eclipses of 810 (21 June or 15 December).

entries.title: Echaid son of Fiachna, king of Ulaid, dies
Law on cattle proclaimed in Munster by Daire and Aduar son of Echen
entries.effect: law: cattle protected (Cain Daire) in Munster

entries.title: Eanred son of Eardwulf becomes king of Northumbria (date uncertain)
entries.note: Wendover makes him follow Aelfwald II; Eardwulf's end is unrecorded.

entries.title: Caliph al-Amin names his son Musa heir in place of his brother al-Ma'mun
entries.effect: civil war looming in the Caliphate

entries.title: Amoroz driven out of Zaragoza by al-Hakam's son Abd al-Rahman, forced into Huesca
entries.effect: Ebro valley back under Cordoba

entries.title: A fireball crosses the sky; Charles thrown from his horse on the march against Godfred
Godfred of the Danes murdered by one of his men; nephew Hemming succeeds, makes peace
entries.effect: Danish threat lifts; the Danish fleet goes home

entries.title: Wilzi take the Elbe fort of Hohbuoki and its garrison
entries.effect: middle Elbe crossing lost

entries.title: Pippin, king of Italy, dies
entries.effect: Frankish war on Venice ends
entries.note: VIII Id. Iul.

entries.title: Cattle plague kills nearly all the army's oxen and rages through every province
entries.effect: murrain realm-wide: carts and ploughs short; meat and hides dear; mobs kill people blamed for spreading 'deadly dust'
entries.note: Agobard tells of a rumour that Grimoald of Benevento sent men to spread poison dust.

entries.title: At Aachen Charles makes peace with Nikephoros, returning Venice, and with al-Hakam
entries.effect: Venice back to Byzantium; peace with Cordoba; Count Haimric freed

entries.title: Corsica ravaged by the Moors a second time
entries.effect: Corsica unsafe

entries.title: Charles orders a fleet built against the Northmen; ship timber gathered
entries.effect: shipbuilding on the rivers to the North Sea; timber and shipwrights in demand; watches in ports and river mouths
entries.note: ARF 811 says it was ordered the year before; the 810 capitulary was for missi sent to the coasts.

entries.title: Eclipse of the sun
entries.note: II Kal. Dec.

entries.title: Three-day fast ordered in Mainz province against plagues on men and beasts
sources: MGH Capit. I no. 127 (Riculf to Egino)
entries.note: Year assigned by Jaffé.

entries.title: Eclipse of the moon
entries.note: XVIII Kal. Ian.

entries.title: Very hard winter; frost closes the roads between Franks and Danes
entries.effect: harsh winter: land routes closed; the Danish peace sworn only on arms until spring

entries.title: Peace with Hemming sworn on the Eider by twelve Frankish and twelve Danish nobles
entries.effect: Franco-Danish peace: the Eider the border; Hedeby trade reopens

entries.title: Tahir ibn al-Husayn routs al-Amin's army at Rayy; its general Ali ibn Isa killed
entries.effect: Abbasid civil war: the Khurasan road closed

entries.title: Haido of Basel, Hugh of Tours and Aio sent to Constantinople; Doge Willeri deposed
entries.effect: Venice's pro-Frankish doge removed

entries.title: Agnello Particiaco becomes doge; the ducal seat settles at Rialto
sources: John the Deacon, Istoria Veneticorum II
entries.effect: new doge; Rialto becomes the centre of Venice
entries.note: Traditional date; the chronicle is of about 1000.

entries.title: Charles divides his treasure; alms for 21 metropolitan sees, Cologne and Mainz among them
entries.note: Also Bordeaux, Tours, Reims, Trier and others.

entries.title: Two eclipses of the sun noted
entries.note: Einhard: frequent eclipses in his last three years.

entries.title: Nuadu, abbot of Armagh, takes the law of Patrick and his shrine to Connacht
entries.effect: law: Cain Patraic in Connacht

entries.title: The Ulaid slaughter a band of heathens
entries.effect: raiders beaten off the Ulster coast

entries.title: A year of prodigies in Ireland: bread bleeds when cut, birds speak
Owain son of Maredudd of Dyfed dies
Ecgberht said to ravage Wales from north to south (?)
An army ravages the Linones beyond the Elbe and rebuilds Hohbuoki
entries.effect: middle Elbe secured

entries.title: A Frankish army sent into Pannonia to settle quarrels between Avars and Slavs
entries.effect: Danube lands policed by the Franks

entries.title: An army sent against the Bretons to punish their breach of faith
entries.effect: war on the Breton coast

entries.title: Nikephoros takes and burns Krum's residence at Pliska
entries.effect: Bulgaria sacked

entries.title: Nikephoros I killed with his army in a Balkan pass; Krum makes his skull a cup
entries.effect: Byzantine army destroyed; Thrace and the Black Sea coast open to the Bulgars
entries.note: 26 July 811 was a Saturday.

entries.title: Fair of Tailtiu not held: no horse or chariot comes, a boycott by the Tallaght community
entries.effect: fair cancelled: no horse or cattle trade at Tailtiu this year
entries.note: The Ui Neill had violated Tallaght's sanctuary. The fair fell at Lughnasa (1 August); AU says it failed on the Saturday, which would be 2 August 811 (?).

entries.title: At Boulogne Charles inspects the new fleet and relights the old Roman lighthouse
entries.effect: the Boulogne light burns at night: a safer approach on the Channel coast; royal fleet based at Boulogne

entries.title: Boulogne capitulary: lords to sail with the fleet; churches not to sell byrnies or swords
entries.effect: law: arms not to leave church stores; three months' food for a campaign from the march

entries.title: Staurakios abdicates; Michael I Rangabe proclaimed emperor
entries.effect: new emperor

entries.title: At Ghent on the Scheldt Charles views the ships built for the fleet
entries.effect: Ghent shipyards busy; a Scheldt fleet base
entries.note: He was back at Aachen about mid-November.

entries.title: Hemming's envoys and Avar and Danube Slav leaders await Charles at Aachen
entries.effect: Danes and Avars at peace with the Franks

entries.title: Charles the Younger, the emperor's eldest son, dies
entries.effect: the heir to Neustria, Frisia and Saxony is gone; Louis sole heir
entries.note: II Non. Dec.

entries.title: Hemming dies; Sigfrid and Anulo fight for the Danish throne; both fall, with 10,940 men
entries.effect: Danish civil war; Anulo's brothers Harald and Reginfrid made kings
entries.note: The ARF puts Hemming's death at the head of 812.

entries.title: Praeceptum pro Hispanis protects Spanish settlers in Septimania
entries.effect: Spanish refugees on the march shielded from counts' exactions

entries.title: Eclipse of the sun in the afternoon
entries.note: ARF: Id. Mai.; the eclipse is usually dated 14 May 812 (?).

entries.title: Krum takes Develtos and deports its people; Thracian towns abandoned in panic
entries.effect: Black Sea coast of Thrace hostile; Anchialos, Berrhoia and Philippopolis emptied

entries.title: Envoys of Michael I at Aachen hail Charles as basileus and take the treaty
entries.effect: peace with Byzantium: Venice and the Dalmatian coast stay Byzantine; the Franks keep Istria

entries.title: Bernard sent to Italy with Wala against a rumoured African and Spanish fleet
Moorish fleet reaches Corsica and Sardinia; the part at Sardinia almost wholly destroyed
entries.effect: Tyrrhenian Sea hostile
entries.note: It is the raiders' Sardinian squadron that was destroyed.

entries.title: A Northman fleet attacks Ireland and is beaten off with heavy losses
entries.effect: raiders checked in Ireland

entries.title: Peace with al-Hakam of Cordoba (kept three years)
entries.effect: Spanish March quiet

entries.title: Peace with Grimoald of Benevento; 25,000 gold solidi paid as tribute
Campaign against the Wilzi; hostages taken
entries.effect: Wilzi quiet for now

entries.title: Ibrahim I ibn al-Aghlab dies; his son Abdallah I succeeds in Ifriqiya
entries.effect: new emir in Ifriqiya

entries.title: The men of Umall defeat a band of heathens; heathens slaughter the Conmaicne
entries.effect: raiders active on the Connacht coast

entries.title: Cobthach son of Mael Duin, king of Loch Lein, slaughters heathens in Munster
entries.effect: raiders in south-west Munster beaten

entries.title: Law of Daire proclaimed in Connacht
entries.effect: law: Cain Daire (cattle) in Connacht

entries.title: The fortress of Degannwy struck by lightning and burned
Disert Diarmata (Castledermot) founded
Danish kings Harald and Reginfrid ask peace and their brother Hemming's return
entries.effect: Danish-Frankish peace holds

entries.title: Al-Ma'mun's generals begin the siege of Baghdad
entries.effect: Baghdad besieged for a year: markets burned, trade in Iraq halted

entries.title: Krum offers peace on the old terms, with sealed passes for merchants; Michael refuses
entries.effect: proposed law: merchants of both sides to carry seals, goods without them forfeit; refusal means war on the Black Sea coast

entries.title: Krum takes Mesembria with its gold, silver and Greek-fire siphons
entries.effect: a Black Sea port lost to the Bulgars
entries.note: Theophanes counts 36 bronze siphons.

entries.title: A comet seen at Constantinople, like two moons joined and then parted
entries.effect: portent

entries.title: Amalarius of Trier and Peter of Nonantola sent to Constantinople to confirm the peace
entries.effect: Frankish-Byzantine peace being ratified

entries.title: Eclipse of the sun
entries.note: Seen at Constantinople; Ann. Laub. 813 note an eclipse, probably this one (?).

entries.title: Aachen portico collapses on Ascension Day; tremors and lightning at the palace (?)
entries.note: Einhard gives no year, only his last years; if 813, Ascension Day was 5 May.

entries.title: Krum defeats Michael I at Versinikia near Adrianople
entries.effect: Thrace overrun by the Bulgars

entries.title: Northmen raid Frisia, carrying off men, women and much booty
entries.effect: Frisian coast raided: captives taken; trade disrupted
entries.note: Moissac codex 2 puts it under 814.

entries.title: Count Irmingar of Ampurias takes 8 Moorish ships off Majorca, freeing 500 Corsicans
entries.effect: Corsican captives freed; Balearic waters fought over

entries.title: In revenge the Moors sack Civitavecchia and Nice; beaten off in Sardinia
entries.effect: Tuscan and Provencal coasts raided

entries.title: The wooden Rhine bridge at Mainz burns down in three hours
entries.effect: Rhine crossing at Mainz by boat only; ferrymen busy
entries.note: Einhard: a year before Charles died; it had taken ten years to build.

entries.title: Leo V defeats a Bulgar army near Mesembria (?)
entries.effect: Bulgar pressure eased
entries.note: 813 or 814; late sources.

entries.title: Heathens slaughter the men of Umall; Dunadach, king of Umall, falls
entries.effect: west Connacht coast hostile

entries.title: Law of Daire proclaimed among the Ui Neill
entries.effect: law: Cain Daire (cattle) in Ui Neill lands

entries.title: Battle between Hywel and Cynan for Gwynedd; Hywel wins
Michael I abdicates and becomes a monk; Leo V the Armenian crowned next day
entries.effect: new emperor

entries.title: Reform councils at Mainz, Reims, Tours, Chalon and Arles
entries.effect: church reform decrees, reported to the September assembly
entries.note: Moissac lists four (no Chalon). No days given.

entries.title: Frankish and Saxon lords and 16 Danish nobles swear peace beyond the Elbe; Hemming returned
entries.effect: Danish-Frankish peace renewed

entries.title: Danish kings Harald and Reginfrid campaign in Vestfold to force its submission
entries.effect: Vestfold at war: Skiringssal market disrupted; Danish overlordship over the Vik
entries.note: ARF: its lords and people refused to submit; it faces the north of Britain.

entries.title: Krum before the walls of Constantinople; wounded in an ambush at a parley; suburbs burned
entries.effect: suburbs and Thracian shore laid waste

entries.title: Aachen assembly: Louis crowned co-emperor; Bernard made king of Italy
entries.effect: succession settled
entries.note: Moissac: September; the day is reconstructed from Thegan's Sunday (11 September 813 was a Sunday) (?).

entries.title: Caliph al-Amin killed as Baghdad falls; al-Ma'mun sole caliph
entries.effect: civil war ends; the caliph stays at Merv; Iraq in disorder
entries.note: Night of 24/25 September 813.

entries.title: Godfred's sons return from exile among the Swedes and drive out Harald and Reginfrid
entries.effect: Danish regime change; Harald flees to the Abodrites

entries.title: Krum takes Adrianople and deports its people beyond the Danube
entries.effect: Thrace emptied; about 10,000 deported

entries.title: Bulgar army ravages Thrace and takes Arkadiopolis with many captives
entries.effect: Thrace unsafe
entries.note: The captives are put at 50,000.

entries.title: Very hard winter
entries.effect: harsh winter: rivers and roads frozen
entries.note: Told after Louis's coronation, so probably the winter of 813/814 (?).

entries.title: Charlemagne dies at Aachen at the third hour and is buried the same day
entries.effect: the realm passes to Louis
entries.note: V Kal. Febr. Einhard: a fever in January, then pleurisy; he died on the seventh day.

entries.title: Louis, told at Doué in Anjou, reaches Aachen 30 days later and takes over
entries.effect: new ruler of every Frankish port
entries.note: ARF: on the 30th day after the death (about 27 February); Ann. Xant.: in March.

entries.title: Krum dies while preparing an assault on Constantinople
entries.effect: Bulgar threat to Constantinople lifts; peace follows under Omurtag

entries.title: Louis receives Leo V's envoys with the confirmed peace and sends his own
entries.effect: Frankish-Byzantine peace ratified: Venice Byzantine and free to trade with both

entries.title: Assembly at Aachen sends missi through the realm to right wrongs
entries.effect: missi hear complaints against officials

entries.title: Pact with Grimoald: Benevento to pay 7,000 solidi every year
Louis sends Lothar to Bavaria and Pippin to Aquitaine as king
entries.effect: new ruler over Aquitaine (Bordeaux)

entries.title: Harald and Reginfrid attack Godfred's sons; Reginfrid and Godfred's eldest son killed
entries.effect: Danish civil war goes on; Godfred's sons hold the kingdom

entries.title: Harald commends himself to Louis and is told to wait in Saxony
entries.effect: Frankish backing for a Danish pretender; border tension

entries.title: Archbishop Wulfred and Bishop Wigberht of Wessex go to Rome
entries.note: ASC year two early; Wulfred came back the next year.

entries.title: Great distress and severe sickness in Ireland
entries.effect: hunger and sickness in Ireland: food dear, crews short

entries.title: Cellach, abbot of Iona, resigns when the church at Kells is finished; Diarmait succeeds
entries.effect: new abbot at hi

entries.title: Law of Ciaran proclaimed at Cruachain by Muirgius, king of Connacht
entries.effect: law: Cain Chiarain in Connacht

entries.title: Leinster civil war: the Ui Cheinnselaig beaten by the sons of Bran
entries.effect: north Leinster dynasty (Liffey country) stronger

entries.title: Great thunder in Wales causes many fires
Gruffydd son of Cyngen of Powys killed by his brother Elisedd; Tryffin son of Rhain dies
Hywel takes Anglesey and drives out Cynan, with heavy losses
entries.effect: Menai and Anglesey waters disturbed

entries.title: Two attempts to cross the frozen Elbe to aid Harald foiled by sudden thaws
entries.effect: Elbe ice unsafe; the army waits until mid-May 815
entries.note: ARF 815: 'that winter'; it may belong to January-February 815.

entries.title: A Saxon and Obodrite army crosses the Eider into Danish land to restore Harald Klak; the Danes will not give battle
entries.effect: war in the Danish borderland this summer: Sliesthorp's road and the Eider unsafe
entries.note: The army reached the district of Sinlendi and went home after seven days with hostages; the sons of Godfred had gathered a fleet of 200 ships off an island and did not come out.

entries.title: Ordinatio imperii at Aachen: Lothar made co-emperor and heir, with sub-kingdoms for Pippin and Louis
entries.effect: the empire's succession set: Aquitaine to Pippin, Bavaria to Louis, the rest to Lothar

entries.title: Thirteen pirate ships from the north beaten off in Flanders and at the Seine mouth; they sack Bouin in Aquitaine
entries.effect: raiders off the Channel and Bay of Biscay coasts this season: coastguards out; the salt coast south of the Loire raided
entries.note: In Flanders they were driven off by the coastguard; at the Seine they lost five men; they went home with great booty from Bouin.

entries.title: A long hard winter: the Rhine, Danube, Elbe and Seine freeze so hard that carts cross on the ice for thirty days
entries.effect: rivers closed to boats for a month; food and firewood dear; the thaw floods villages along the Rhine
entries.note: The autumn sowing was already spoiled by rain. When the ice broke up it did great damage to villages on the Rhine.

entries.title: Famine and an epidemic in many parts of Francia; a hailstorm destroys crops
entries.effect: grain dear across Francia; deaths from sickness
entries.note: The ARF set it among the year's portents, among them an earthquake at Aachen.

entries.title: The Danish king Harald Klak is baptised at Mainz with his wife and many followers, and given Rüstringen in Frisia
entries.effect: a Christian Danish king holds Rüstringen; Ansgar goes north with him: a mission at the Danish border
entries.note: Ermold places the baptism at Ingelheim's palace, with St Alban's at Mainz as the church; the day is often given as 24 June (?).

entries.title: An Aghlabid army from Ifriqiya lands at Mazara: the Muslim conquest of Sicily begins
entries.effect: war in Sicily for decades: the central Mediterranean unsafe for Byzantine shipping
entries.note: The fleet sailed from Sousse in mid-June 827 at the call of the rebel Euphemios. Palermo fell in 831.

entries.title: Harald Klak driven out of the Danish kingdom by the sons of Godfred
entries.effect: the sons of Godfred rule the Danes alone; Horik becomes the chief king

entries.title: Ansgar sails for Birka with merchants; robbed by pirates on the way, he reaches Birka on foot and is allowed to preach
entries.effect: the first Christian mission at Birka; the Swedish king's prefect Herigar builds a church
entries.note: Rimbert gives no year; the Swedish envoys came to Louis in 829 and Ansgar stayed about a year and a half (829-831).

entries.title: Louis the Pious's elder sons rise against him and Empress Judith; Louis is held at Compiègne
entries.effect: civil strife in Francia: the court in turmoil; restored to power in the autumn

entries.title: Hamburg made an archbishopric for the mission to the north, with Ansgar as archbishop
entries.effect: a church base at the Elbe for the Danes and Svear; Hamburg grows as a port
entries.note: Consecrated 831 or 832 (?); Gregory IV gave him the pallium.

entries.title: The 'Field of Lies' near Colmar: Louis the Pious's army deserts him to his sons and he is deposed
entries.effect: Lothar rules the empire for the winter; civil war in Francia; the coasts left unwatched
entries.note: The armies faced each other from about 24 June; the desertion is usually put on 29-30 June.

entries.title: Louis the Pious restored to his arms and throne at Saint-Denis
entries.effect: the old emperor rules again; Lothar withdraws to Italy

entries.title: A Danish fleet ravages Frisia, comes by Utrecht to Dorestad and destroys everything, killing and carrying off people
entries.effect: raid on dorestad: the emporium burned, people killed and taken; Utrecht threatened
entries.note: The first of four years running of raids on Dorestad (834-837). The AB put it in the same year as Louis's restoration; the Xanten annals say the Northmen came 'unexpectedly'.

entries.title: The Northmen ravage Dorestad again and lay waste Frisia
entries.effect: raid on dorestad: the market burned again
entries.note: The same year the island monastery of Noirmoutier was attacked (AB 835).

entries.title: Northmen plunder the island monastery of Noirmoutier (Herio), the salt island at the Loire's mouth
entries.effect: raid on herio: the salt island plundered; the monks begin to leave
entries.note: Ermentarius tells of yearly raids on the island from about 819; the monks left for good in 836.

entries.title: The Northmen burn Antwerp and the emporium of Witla at the Meuse mouth, and raid Dorestad a third time
entries.effect: raids on witla and andoverpis: both burned; dorestad raided again
entries.note: Witla (near Rotterdam/Voorne) is not named again after this.

entries.title: A comet seen for 25 days in Virgo (Halley's comet)
entries.effect: news only: the emperor fears it and orders prayers and alms
entries.note: Seen from Easter week; Halley's comet passed closest to the earth on 10-11 April 837.

entries.title: Northmen fall on Walcheren, kill Count Eggihard and Hemming son of Halfdan, then take tribute from Dorestad
entries.effect: raid on walichrum: many taken captive; dorestad pays tribute; Louis gives up his journey to Italy to guard the coast
entries.note: xv kal. Iul. (17 June). Louis gathered an army at Nijmegen; the Northmen left at once.

entries.title: King Ecgberht of Wessex defeats a great Viking fleet and the Cornish together at Hingston Down
entries.effect: Cornwall under Wessex: its tin in West Saxon hands
entries.note: The ASC's years run two or three behind here.

entries.title: A storm flood breaks over Frisia: the sea covers almost all of it and 2,437 people are counted drowned
entries.effect: storm surge: the terp country under water; dikes and harbours damaged, cattle and stores lost
entries.note: Told under 839, on the feast of St Stephen (26 December 838); the count of the drowned is the annal's own.
