entries.title: Byzantine envoys reach Louis at Ingelheim with men who call themselves 'Rhos'; they prove to be Swedes, and are held
entries.effect: news: the Rus' way home from Constantinople is blocked by wild peoples; the Svear trade east by the rivers
entries.note: The first record of the Rus. xv kal. Iun. (18 May). Louis suspected them of being spies.

entries.title: Emperor Louis the Pious dies on an island in the Rhine near Ingelheim
entries.effect: civil war among his sons follows; the coasts are left to the raiders

entries.title: Northmen under Oscherus come up the Seine, sack Rouen and burn the abbey of Jumièges
entries.effect: raid on rotomagus: the town plundered and burned; Saint-Wandrille ransoms itself
entries.note: The Fontenelle chronicle puts their stay on the Seine in the second half of May.

entries.title: Battle of Fontenoy: Charles the Bald and Louis the German defeat Lothar in a great slaughter
entries.effect: the Frankish nobility bled; the kingdom split in three

entries.title: Northmen build a ship-fort (longphort) at Dublin and winter there
entries.effect: a Norse base at duiblinn: slaves, silver and raids out of it all year round
entries.note: The same year a longphort was made at Linn Duachaill (Annagassan).

entries.title: Lothar grants Walcheren and the neighbouring places to the Danish exile Harald, to keep other raiders out
entries.effect: walichrum held by a Danish lord: his men plunder Christians as they please
entries.note: The AB call it a deed 'to be detested'.

entries.title: Oaths of Strasbourg: Louis the German and Charles the Bald swear alliance, each in the other's tongue
entries.effect: the two younger brothers allied against Lothar
entries.note: Nithard gives the oaths' texts in early French and German.

entries.title: A Northman fleet sacks Quentovic at dawn, killing and carrying off its people and sparing only the houses that paid
entries.effect: raid on quentovic: the mint and port plundered; the Channel crossing unsafe
entries.note: The AB tell of the dawn attack; Nithard adds that they crossed the sea and plundered Hamwic (Hamwig) and Nordhunnwig, perhaps Norwich (?), in the same way.

entries.title: Northmen, led by the rebel count Lambert, storm Nantes on St John's day and kill Bishop Gunhard in his cathedral
entries.effect: raid on namnetis: the town plundered and many killed; the raiders then winter on Noirmoutier, the first wintering in Francia
entries.note: The AB seem to call the fleet Westfaldingi, men of Vestfold (?). They wintered on the island and brought their households, 'as if to stay for ever'.

entries.title: Kenneth son of Alpin, king of Dal Riata, becomes king of the Picts as well (c. 843)
sources: Chronicle of the Kings of Alba
entries.effect: Scots and Picts under one king: the kingdom later called Alba
entries.note: The year is reckoned back from his death in 858, said to be in the sixteenth year of his reign over the Picts.

entries.title: Treaty of Verdun: the Frankish empire divided into west (Charles), middle (Lothar, with Frisia and Italy) and east (Louis)
entries.effect: three kingdoms: Frisia, the Rhine delta, the Meuse, Cologne and Italy to Lothar; Flanders, Neustria, the Loire and Aquitaine to Charles; Saxony, Mainz and the east to Louis
entries.note: The day is not recorded; early August 843.

entries.title: A Viking fleet comes up the Guadalquivir and takes Seville; the emir's army defeats them at Tablada in November
entries.effect: raid in al-Andalus: Seville plundered for weeks; afterwards Cordoba builds a fleet and an arsenal at Seville
entries.note: They had raided Lisbon and Cadiz on the way. The Arab writers call them al-majus. The days vary between the sources; the defeat is usually put on 11 November 844.

entries.title: Ragnar's fleet of 120 ships comes up the Seine and sacks Paris on Easter Sunday; Charles the Bald pays 7,000 pounds of silver for them to go
entries.effect: raid on parisius: the town and its abbeys plundered; rotomagus raided on the way; a great tribute in silver goes north
entries.note: The first tribute paid to Vikings by a Frankish king. On the way home many of them died of sickness (the AB and the Translatio see God's punishment).

entries.title: A Danish fleet takes Hamburg by surprise and burns it, church, books and all; Ansgar flees with the relics
entries.effect: Hamburg burned: the mission's base lost; the see is joined to Bremen (848)
entries.note: The AB say King Horik sent 600 ships up the Elbe that year and the Saxons beat them; whether this was the same fleet is not certain.

entries.title: The Viking leader Turgéis captured by Máel Sechnaill and drowned in Loch Uair
entries.effect: the Norse of the Midlands lose their leader

entries.title: Danish pirates burn Dorestad and two other villages while Lothar watches from Nijmegen and cannot stop them
entries.effect: dorestad burned again; Frisia pays tribute
entries.note: The AB of 846-847 tell of Danes taking tribute from Frisia and holding Dorestad and the Betuwe; the Xanten annals have the burning in sight of Lothar at Nijmegen.

entries.title: Arab raiders from Africa land at Ostia, plunder St Peter's and St Paul's outside the walls of Rome
entries.effect: raid at Rome: the basilicas stripped of their treasure; the Leonine wall begun around St Peter's
entries.note: The day is usually given as 23 August (?).

entries.title: Lothar grants Dorestad and other counties to the Danish chief Rorik, who had taken them with his fleet, in return for his fealty
entries.effect: dorestad held by a Danish lord for the emperor: other raiders kept off, his own men paid
entries.note: Rorik held Dorestad on and off until about 873; he was to defend the coast against other Danes.

entries.title: King Horik lets Ansgar build a church at Sliesthorp, the port where merchants from Dorestad and Hamburg come
entries.effect: a church and priest at sliesthorp: Christian merchants more willing to come
entries.note: Rimbert: before it, Christian traders from Dorestad and Hamburg were afraid to come. The year is about 850 (?).

entries.title: Heathens winter on Thanet for the first time; 350 ships storm Canterbury and London; King Æthelwulf beats them at Aclea
entries.effect: raid on lundenwic and Canterbury: both stormed; the Mercian king put to flight; the raiders now winter in Kent
entries.note: Some manuscripts have Sheppey for Thanet. The wintering may be that of 850/851.

entries.title: Horik I and most of the Danish royal house fall in a civil war with his nephew Guthorm
entries.effect: the Danes without a strong king: the boy Horik II is made king; the church at Sliesthorp is shut for a time

entries.title: The Svear under King Olof take Seeburg in Courland and besiege Apulia until the Curonians pay and submit
entries.effect: grobin taken and burned; the Curonians pay tribute to the Svear
entries.note: Rimbert says the Curonians had thrown off Swedish rule, and that the Danes had tried and failed before. Seeburg is usually taken to be Grobina; the year is c. 854 (?).

entries.title: Danish pirates sail through the Straits of Gibraltar, raid Spain and Morocco, winter in the Camargue and go on to Italy (859-861)
entries.effect: raiders in the Mediterranean: Algeciras, Nekor, the Rhone towns and Pisa plundered; ships of al-Andalus and Provence at risk
entries.note: The two leaders are named by later writers (Dudo, the Irish Fragmentary Annals); the story that they took Luna for Rome is Dudo's.

entries.title: A very hard, long winter, with snow and frost from November to April; in Italy the sea freezes along the coast
entries.effect: rivers and harbours frozen: no sailing; wine, food and firewood dear
entries.note: The Fulda annals say merchants went to Venice over the ice with horses and carts. The AB put the winter's end in April.

entries.title: A Rus fleet of 200 ships attacks Constantinople while the emperor is away, plundering the suburbs and the islands
entries.effect: the Rus raid Byzantium: the Bosporus unsafe; the Rus soon send envoys and are baptised (Photios)
entries.note: The Brussels chronicle gives 18 June; the Rus left in early August.

entries.title: The Primary Chronicle's year for Rurik and his brothers being called from over the sea to rule the Slavs and Finns; Rurik settles at Ladoga, later Novgorod
entries.effect: a Rus prince at aldeigjuborg: tribute in furs taken from the Slavs and Finns
entries.note: Written down about 250 years later; the date is the chronicle's own (AM 6370), and the story is partly legend. The Hypatian copy has Rurik first at Ladoga.

entries.title: The Danes sack Dorestad once more and sail up the Rhine towards Cologne
entries.effect: raid on dorestad: the last time it is named as a trading place; trade moves to Tiel and Deventer
entries.note: Among the first events of 863 in the AB. Dorestad's river was silting up and the Rhine's main stream moving south to the Lek and Waal.

entries.title: Edict of Pîtres: a new coinage from ten mints only, fortified bridges on the rivers, and no arms or horses to be sold to the Northmen
entries.effect: coin: old pennies exchanged for the new by 11 November; law: selling arms or horses to Northmen punished by death; a fortified bridge built at Pont-de-l'Arche to close the Seine
entries.note: The ten named mints include Quentovic, Rouen and the palace.

entries.title: A great heathen army comes to England and winters in East Anglia, where the people make peace and give them horses
entries.effect: a great army in England: East Anglia buys peace with horses; war for years to come
entries.note: The ASC's year began in the autumn, so its 866 entry tells of autumn 865.

entries.title: The great army crosses the Humber and takes York on All Saints' Day
entries.effect: eoforwic held by the Danes: its trade and mint theirs
entries.note: Northumbria was split between the rival kings Osberht and Ælla.

entries.title: The Northumbrian kings Osberht and Ælla storm York together and both are killed
entries.effect: Northumbria under the Danes, with an English puppet king (Ecgberht) north of the Tyne
entries.note: HR: xii kal. Apr.

entries.title: The great army winters at Thetford; King Edmund of East Anglia fights them and is killed, and they take the kingdom
sources: Abbo of Fleury, Passio S. Eadmundi
entries.effect: East Anglia under the Danes: gipeswic's trade in their hands
entries.note: Abbo's later Passio has Edmund martyred, shot with arrows; the cult made him St Edmund.

entries.title: Amlaíb and Ímar besiege Dumbarton Rock for four months and destroy it; next year 200 ships bring Britons, Picts and Angles to Dublin as slaves
entries.effect: a great haul of slaves at duiblinn: slaves cheap there next year

entries.title: Treaty of Meerssen: Charles the Bald and Louis the German divide Lotharingia, Frisia and the Meuse between them
entries.effect: the middle kingdom gone: the Meuse and Frisia split between west and east; tolls and lords change

entries.title: Battle of Ashdown: King Æthelred and his brother Alfred defeat the Danish army
entries.effect: Wessex holds; nine battles that year
entries.note: The day is from Asser's account and the ASC's reckoning; the year of battles went on with Basing and Meretun.

entries.title: King Æthelred of Wessex dies after Easter; his brother Alfred becomes king
entries.effect: new king of Wessex: Alfred buys peace with the army that autumn
entries.note: Æthelred's death is traditionally put on 23 April 871.

entries.title: Battle of Hafrsfjord: Harald Fairhair defeats the kings of the west and rules most of the Norwegian coast (traditional date)
entries.effect: one king over the western coast: chiefs leave for Iceland and the isles (the sagas' story)
entries.note: The date 872 comes from Icelandic reckoning of the 12th-13th centuries; many historians put the battle about 885-900.

entries.title: The great army winters at Repton and drives King Burgred out of Mercia; he goes to Rome and the Danes set up Ceolwulf
entries.effect: Mercia under a Danish-made king; London's mint and trade disturbed
entries.note: The army had wintered at London in 871-872, where the Mercians bought peace.

entries.title: Ingólfr Arnarson settles at Reykjavík: the beginning of the settlement of Iceland (traditional date)
entries.effect: Iceland settled from Norway and the isles: a new land wanting iron, timber, grain and malt, and selling wool and walrus
entries.note: Ari puts the beginning of the settlement about 870, Landnámabók has Ingólfr settle in 874; the 'settlement layer' of volcanic ash under the first farms is dated by Greenland ice cores to the 870s.

entries.title: Halfdan shares out the land of Northumbria and his men begin to plough and live there
entries.effect: Danish settlers in Yorkshire: a Danish kingdom at eoforwic, trading with Dublin and the Danes
entries.note: The first record of a Viking army settling down in England.

entries.title: The Danish army takes Chippenham by stealth after Twelfth Night; Alfred escapes into the Somerset marshes at Athelney
entries.effect: Wessex overrun: many flee overseas; the south cut off from its king
entries.note: 'At midwinter after Twelfth Night'.

entries.title: Battle of Edington: Alfred defeats Guthrum, who gives hostages and is baptised three weeks later
entries.effect: Wessex saved; Guthrum's army leaves and settles East Anglia (880); the boundary later set by treaty
entries.note: In the seventh week after Easter (Easter was 23 March). Guthrum was baptised at Aller as Æthelstan, and his chrism loosed at Wedmore.

entries.title: The great army crosses from England to Francia and winters at Ghent, raiding Flanders and the Scheldt
entries.effect: raid on ganda: the abbey and the town held as a winter camp; the lands round plundered for a year
entries.note: The ASC says they stayed at Ghent for a year.

entries.title: A Viking army crushes the Saxons in a winter battle; Duke Brun, two bishops and twelve counts fall
entries.effect: Saxony's leaders killed: the Elbe lands unguarded

entries.title: Battle of Saucourt: King Louis III defeats a Viking army in Vimeu
entries.effect: the raiders turn east, to the Meuse and Rhine
entries.note: The Old High German Ludwigslied sings of the victory.

entries.title: From their camp at Elsloo on the Meuse the Northmen burn Liège, Maastricht, Cologne and Bonn, and stable horses in the palace chapel at Aachen
entries.effect: raids on colonia and the Meuse towns: the whole valley plundered for the winter; Trier sacked on 5 April 882

entries.title: The Primary Chronicle's year for Oleg taking Kiev and making it the Rus capital, 'the mother of Rus cities'
entries.effect: the way from the Varangians to the Greeks under one Rus prince: furs and slaves down the Dnieper
entries.note: A chronicle date written down much later.

entries.title: At Asselt, Charles the Fat buys peace: Godfrid is baptised and given Frisia as a fief, Sigfrid takes thousands of pounds of silver
entries.effect: Frisia held by a Danish duke: raiders kept off, but his men lord it
entries.note: The Fulda annals put the payment at about 2,080 pounds of gold and silver (?).

entries.title: Duke Godfrid of Frisia killed at Herispich in the Betuwe by the emperor's men
entries.effect: the Danish rule of Frisia ends; Frisia back under the East Frankish king

entries.title: Siege of Paris: a huge Viking fleet under Sigfrid besieges the city for eleven months; Count Odo and Bishop Gozlin hold it
entries.effect: the Seine closed above Rouen for a year; in November 886 Charles the Fat pays 700 pounds and lets them winter in Burgundy
entries.note: Abbo, an eyewitness, speaks of 700 ships, perhaps too many (?).

entries.title: Alfred occupies London and gives it to Ealdorman Æthelred of Mercia; all the English not under the Danes accept him
entries.effect: lundenwic moves inside the old Roman walls (Lundenburh); the treaty with Guthrum fixes the Danelaw border along the Lea and Watling Street
entries.note: The treaty of Alfred and Guthrum is undated; it belongs between 878 and 890.

entries.title: Charles the Fat deposed at Tribur; Arnulf of Carinthia is made king in the east and the empire breaks up for good
entries.effect: new kings everywhere: Odo in the west (888), Arnulf in the east; each kingdom fights the raiders alone
entries.note: Charles died on 13 January 888.

entries.title: Ohthere of Hålogaland and Wulfstan tell King Alfred of their voyages: north to the White Sea, south to Skiringssal and Hedeby, and from Hedeby to Truso
entries.effect: news of the northern sea-roads: the days' sailing from Hålogaland to Skiringssal (a month) and on to Hedeby (five days), and from Hedeby to Truso (seven days and nights)
entries.note: Added to the Old English Orosius made at Alfred's court; the visit is undated, about 890 (?). Ohthere brought the king walrus tusks and told of the Sami's tribute in furs, feathers, whalebone and ship-ropes.

entries.title: King Arnulf storms the Viking camp on the Dyle near Leuven and destroys the army
entries.effect: the great army broken on the Continent: it crosses to England the next year
entries.note: The day is usually given as 1 September (?).

entries.title: The army from Boulogne crosses to Kent with 250 ships and builds a fort at Appledore; Hæsten comes into the Thames with 80 ships to Milton
entries.effect: war in England for four years: Kent, the Thames and the Severn raided
entries.note: The ASC's year began in the autumn.

entries.title: Alfred has longships built against the raiders, nearly twice as long as theirs, some with sixty oars, swifter, steadier and higher
entries.effect: English warships on the south coast: raiders' ships taken in the estuaries
entries.note: The ASC says they were built 'neither on the Frisian pattern nor the Danish, but as he himself thought most useful'.

entries.title: King Alfred dies; his son Edward the Elder succeeds
entries.effect: new king of the Anglo-Saxons: Edward and his sister Æthelflæd win back the Danelaw

entries.title: The men of Brega and Leinster drive the Norse out of Dublin; they leave many of their ships behind
entries.effect: no Norse at duiblinn: its slave and silver trade stops; the exiles go to Wales, Man and the Wirral
entries.note: They came back in 917.

entries.title: The Primary Chronicle's year for Oleg's campaign against Constantinople with 2,000 ships, ending in tribute and a trade agreement
entries.effect: Rus merchants given food, baths and ship's gear at Constantinople (the chronicle's terms)
entries.note: The Greek sources say nothing of it; the treaty of 911 is better grounded.

entries.title: Battle of Tettenhall: the West Saxons and Mercians destroy a Northumbrian Danish army; its kings Eowils and Halfdan are killed
entries.effect: the Danes of York broken: the Midlands open to the English reconquest
entries.note: Æthelweard gives 5 August.

entries.title: Oleg's envoys sign a treaty with the emperors Leo and Alexander: rules for Rus merchants at Constantinople, shipwrecks, slaves and crimes
entries.effect: law: Rus merchants trade at Constantinople under treaty; a wrecked ship's goods to be returned; runaway slaves sent back
entries.note: The chronicle gives the treaty's text and its date, 2 September, indiction 15; the text is thought to be a translation of a real Greek document.

entries.title: King Charles the Simple grants Rouen and the lands round the lower Seine to the Viking leader Rollo, who is baptised (traditional date)
sources: charter of Charles the Simple, 14 March 918
entries.effect: a Northman count holds rotomagus for the king: the Seine closed to other raiders; Rouen grows as a port trading with England and the north
entries.note: The meeting at Saint-Clair and the year 911 are Dudo's (about 1015); the charter of 918 speaks of land given to 'the Northmen of the Seine, that is Rollo and his companions'.

entries.title: A Rus fleet of 500 ships passes the Khazars by the Don and Volga and ravages the shores of the Caspian; on the way back most are killed
entries.effect: the Caspian coast raided: the Khazar road for Rus traders closed for a time
entries.note: Al-Mas'udi dates it after AH 300 (912-913). The Khazar king let them through for half the booty; his Muslim guard fell on them on their return.

entries.title: Sihtric grandson of Ímar retakes Dublin for the Norse; his kinsman Ragnall takes Waterford
entries.effect: duiblinn Norse again: the slave trade and raids out of it resume; the Irish king Niall Glúndub killed outside it in 919

entries.title: Æthelflæd, Lady of the Mercians, dies at Tamworth; the people of York had offered to submit to her
entries.effect: Mercia taken over by King Edward: one English kingdom south of the Humber
entries.note: She had refounded Chester's defences in 907.

entries.title: The caliph's envoy Ibn Fadlan reaches the Volga Bulghars; he sees the Rus merchants there and a Rus chief's ship-burial
entries.effect: news: the Bulghar king turns to Baghdad; Rus traders sell slaves and furs for dirhams on the Volga
entries.note: The embassy left Baghdad on 21 June 921. Ibn Fadlan describes the Rus' trade in slave girls and sable for silver, and their custom of stringing green glass beads.

entries.title: Æthelstan takes York; at Eamont King Constantine of Alba, Hywel of the Welsh, Owain of Gwent and Ealdred of Bamburgh submit to him
sources: William of Malmesbury, Gesta regum ii
entries.effect: eoforwic under the English king: one kingdom of England for the first time

entries.title: Æthelstan's laws at Grately: one coinage throughout his realm, moneyers named for each town, and no buying worth over 20 pence outside a town
entries.effect: law: trade in towns before witnesses; one coin; London has 8 moneyers, Canterbury 7, Winchester 6, Southampton 2
entries.note: The code is undated; usually put about 926-930.

entries.title: Abd al-Rahman III takes the title of caliph at Cordoba
entries.effect: al-Andalus a caliphate in its own right: a rich market for slaves, furs and arms from the north

entries.title: The Althing, the general assembly of Iceland, first meets at Þingvellir with one law for the whole land (traditional date)
entries.effect: Iceland's law and courts in one place each summer: a market for goods brought from Norway
entries.note: Ari reckons it sixty years after the settlement began. It met in June.

entries.title: King Henry I of the East Franks defeats the Danes and makes their king Gnupa at Hedeby pay tribute and be baptised
entries.effect: sliesthorp under a German overlord: tribute paid; a mission returns
entries.note: Gnupa's family left runestones near Hedeby.

entries.title: Otto I crowned king of the East Franks at Aachen
entries.effect: a strong Saxon king: Frisia, the Rhine and the Meuse under one ruler; trade through Saxony grows

entries.title: Battle of Brunanburh: Æthelstan and Edmund defeat Olaf of Dublin, Constantine of Alba and Owain of Strathclyde in a great slaughter
entries.effect: the alliance of Dublin and the north broken: England holds together
entries.note: The ASC tells it in a poem; the place is unknown, the Wirral is likeliest. The season is not recorded (?).

entries.title: The Eldgjá fissure eruption in Iceland pours out the largest lava flood of historic times; a haze dims the sun in Europe
entries.effect: farms in south Iceland buried under lava and ash; a cold summer in 940 across the north
entries.note: Dated by ice cores and tree rings to 939-940. The Irish annals of 939 tell of the sun like blood from morning to midday.

entries.title: King Æthelstan dies; Olaf Guthfrithson of Dublin takes York and the Danish Midlands from his brother Edmund
entries.effect: eoforwic ruled from Dublin again: the York-Dublin trade road open; Edmund wins it back by 944
entries.note: The ASC's years run a year late here.

entries.title: Prince Igor's Rus fleet attacks Constantinople and the Bithynian coast; the Byzantines burn many ships with Greek fire
entries.effect: raid on the Byzantine shores: Rus trade with Constantinople stopped until the treaty of 944
entries.note: Liudprand's stepfather saw the captives beheaded.

entries.title: Igor's treaty with Byzantium: Rus ships must carry the prince's charter, merchants stay in the St Mamas quarter and may buy silk only up to 50 gold coins' worth
entries.effect: law: Rus merchants trade at Constantinople again, under a licence and a limit on silk
entries.note: The chronicle gives the text, of 944 or 945.

entries.title: Bishops of Schleswig, Ribe and Aarhus sit at the synod of Ingelheim: the first sees in Denmark
sources: Acts of the synod of Ingelheim (MGH Const. I)
entries.effect: churches at sliesthorp and ripa: German and Frisian merchants welcome
entries.note: The synod met on 7 June 948.

entries.title: The Northumbrians drive out Eric (Bloodaxe), the last king of York; he is killed at Stainmore and King Eadred takes Northumbria
entries.effect: eoforwic English for good: the York-Dublin kingdom ends; York's trade turns south and over the North Sea
entries.note: That he was Eric Bloodaxe son of Harald Fairhair is the later sagas' identification.

entries.title: Battle of the Lechfeld: Otto I destroys the Magyar army near Augsburg
entries.effect: news only: the Magyar raids on the west end; the Danube road opens
entries.note: St Lawrence's day.

entries.title: Princess Olga of Kiev is received at the Great Palace in Constantinople
entries.effect: Kiev and Byzantium at peace: Rus merchants welcome
entries.note: The receptions were on 9 September and 18 October; the year is 957, or 946 by another reckoning (?).

entries.title: King Gorm the Old is buried in the great mound at Jelling (dated by its timbers)
sources: dendrochronology: the North Mound's chamber, felled 958
entries.effect: Harald Bluetooth king of the Danes
entries.note: The chamber timbers were felled in the winter of 958/959; that it was Gorm's grave is likely, not proven.

entries.title: Nikephoros Phokas takes Chandax: Crete back in Byzantine hands after some 135 years as a corsairs' emirate
entries.effect: the Aegean safer for shipping: the slave raids from Crete end

entries.title: Harald Bluetooth is baptised after the priest Poppo carries hot iron unharmed, and orders the Danes to be Christian
entries.effect: the Danish realm Christian: churches in its ports; German merchants and clergy welcome
entries.note: Widukind wrote about 967; 'about 965' is the usual date. The larger Jelling stone says Harald 'won all Denmark and Norway and made the Danes Christian'.

entries.title: Ibrahim ibn Yaqub of Tortosa travels in the north: at Mainz he sees Samarkand dirhams and eastern spices; he finds Hedeby poor and its people heathen
entries.effect: news: eastern silver and pepper, ginger and cloves reach the Rhine; slaves sold from the Slav lands to al-Andalus
entries.note: He saw Samanid coins of 913-915 at Mainz. Only extracts of his account survive, and the Hedeby passage (from al-Qazwini) may belong to another visit.

entries.title: The Danevirke strengthened: a connecting wall built to join Hedeby's rampart to the main wall (dated by its timbers)
entries.effect: the Danish border closed by a wall: the land road south runs through the Danevirke's gate

entries.title: Svyatoslav of Kiev breaks the Khazar kaganate: Sarkel taken, Itil and Samandar sacked
entries.effect: the Khazar toll on the Volga gone: the river road to the Caspian disrupted for years
entries.note: The chronicle puts the war on the Khazars in 965; Ibn Hawqal says the Rus sacked Itil and Bulghar in 358 AH (968-969).

entries.title: The Fatimids take Egypt and found Cairo beside Fustat
entries.effect: Egypt under a new caliphate: the Red Sea and Mediterranean trade turns towards Cairo

entries.title: King Edgar crowned at Bath; afterwards at Chester six kings come to him and pledge to be his allies by land and sea
entries.effect: the court at legacaestir: demand for wine and fine goods; the Irish Sea at peace
entries.note: Whitsun. John of Worcester (12th century) has eight kings row Edgar on the Dee.

entries.title: Edgar's coin reform: one design of penny for all England, struck by named moneyers in many towns and called in every few years
sources: numismatic: Edgar's Reform type (Dolley & Metcalf 1961; Naismith, MEC 8)
entries.effect: coin: old pennies must be exchanged for the new type at the mints; foreign coin reminted
entries.note: Dated by coin study, about 973; later issues changed about every six years.

entries.title: Otto II storms the Danevirke and sets a garrison in the Schleswig march; the Danes take it back in 983
entries.effect: war on the Danish border: the road to sliesthorp closed this season

entries.title: Birka is abandoned in the later 10th century; a new royal town, Sigtuna, is laid out on Mälaren about 980
sources: archaeology: Birka's last coins and finds (Ambrosiani)
entries.effect: birka's trade moves to Sigtuna; the land rising makes the old channels shallow
entries.note: No record says why Birka ended; the falling-off of eastern silver and the rising land are the usual reasons given.

entries.title: Viking raids begin again: Southampton sacked and most of its people killed or taken, Thanet ravaged, Cheshire raided by a fleet from the north
entries.effect: raids on hamwic and legacaestir: the towns plundered; the second Viking age in England begins

entries.title: Battle of Tara: Máel Sechnaill defeats the Norse of Dublin; King Amlaíb Cuarán goes to Iona and dies there
entries.effect: Dublin under the Irish high king: hostages and slaves freed; Dublin pays tribute

entries.title: Harald Bluetooth builds the ring fortresses: Trelleborg, Fyrkat, Aggersborg and Nonnebakken (dated by their timbers)
entries.effect: royal forts guard the roads and fjords: the king's men and tolls everywhere
entries.note: Built within a few years and soon left; the Ravning bridge over the Vejle valley is of the same time (979-980).

entries.title: The great Slav rising: the Lutici and Obodrites destroy Havelberg and Brandenburg and burn Hamburg
entries.effect: the Slav lands free of German rule: churches burned, the Elbe border unsafe, Hamburg burned
entries.note: Thietmar dates the fall of Havelberg to 29 June and Brandenburg three days later.

entries.title: Erik the Red leads settlers from Iceland to Greenland; of 25 ships, 14 arrive (traditional date)
entries.effect: Greenland settled: walrus ivory, walrus-hide rope and white falcons for iron, timber and grain
entries.note: Ari: fourteen or fifteen years before Christianity came to Iceland, i.e. 985 or 986.

entries.title: Vladimir of Kiev campaigns against the Volga Bulghars and makes peace 'until stone floats and hops sink'
entries.effect: peace on the Volga: Rus and Bulghar merchants trade freely
entries.note: The chronicle's date and words.

entries.title: Harald Bluetooth dies of wounds after his son Sweyn Forkbeard rises against him; Sweyn becomes king
entries.effect: Sweyn Forkbeard king of the Danes
entries.note: The year is 986 or 987; Adam says he died at Jumne (Wolin) among the Slavs.

entries.title: Vladimir of Kiev is baptised, marries the emperor's sister Anna and has the people of Kiev baptised in the Dnieper; he sends 6,000 Varangians to Basil II
entries.effect: the Rus Christian and allied to Byzantium: the Varangian Guard formed; Scandinavians go to Constantinople to serve
entries.note: The baptism is put in 987-989 by different sources.

entries.title: Olaf's fleet of 93 ships ravages Folkestone, Sandwich and Ipswich; Ealdorman Byrhtnoth is killed at Maldon; the first great tribute, 10,000 pounds, is paid
entries.effect: raid on gipeswic; the danegeld begins: silver flows from England to the Danes
entries.note: The Ely calendar gives 10 or 11 August. That Olaf was Olaf Tryggvason rests on the A text's naming.

entries.title: Basil II grants Venice a chrysobull: lower tolls for Venetian ships at Abydos and Constantinople, in return for carrying troops
sources: chrysobull of Basil II and Constantine VIII (992)
entries.effect: law: Venetian merchants pay less at the Dardanelles and the capital; Venice's eastern trade grows

entries.title: Olaf and Sweyn come to London with 94 ships and try to burn it; the townsmen drive them off; the army is paid 16,000 pounds
entries.effect: London holds; the coasts of Essex, Kent, Sussex and Hampshire ravaged; a great tribute paid
entries.note: On the Nativity of St Mary.

entries.title: Olaf Tryggvason comes to Norway and is made king after the fall of Jarl Hákon; he presses the Norwegians to be baptised
entries.effect: a Christian king in Norway; trade at Nidaros (Trondheim), which he founds

entries.title: King Olof Skötkonung has the first Swedish coins struck at Sigtuna, copied from English pennies
entries.effect: coin: royal pennies at Sigtuna; English silver from the danegeld in the north
entries.note: Dated by coin study to about 995.

entries.title: The first coins of Dublin are struck under King Sihtric Silkbeard, copied from Æthelred's pennies
entries.effect: coin: Dublin pennies; silver by weight still used too
entries.note: Dated by coin study to about 997.

entries.title: The Althing decides that all Icelanders shall be Christian, though eating horse, exposing children and private sacrifice are still allowed
entries.effect: Iceland Christian by law: its people welcome in Christian ports
entries.note: Ari says it was in the summer that Olaf Tryggvason fell, so 1000; it may have been 999 (?).

entries.title: Islamic silver stops reaching the Baltic: the last dirhams in northern hoards are of the 1010s; German and English pennies take their place
sources: numismatic: the dirham hoards of the Baltic (Noonan; Kovalev and Kaelin)
entries.effect: silver from the east dries up: furs and slaves fetch German and English coin instead; the Volga road loses its draw
entries.note: A slow change dated by coin study, from about 965 to 1015; the Samanid mines' decline is the usual reason given.

entries.title: Leif Eriksson sails from Greenland to lands in the west, Helluland, Markland and Vinland, and builds houses there for a winter (about 1000)
entries.effect: news: timber and grapes in a land west of Greenland; a few voyages follow
entries.note: The sagas were written down about two hundred years later; Adam (about 1075) had heard of Vinland from the Danish king.

entries.title: London's toll rules: at Billingsgate a small boat pays a halfpenny, a sailing ship a penny, a keel or hulk fourpence; men of Rouen, Flanders, Ponthieu, Normandy and France show their goods; the emperor's men trade like Londoners
entries.effect: law: tolls at lundenwic by size of ship; the men of Rouen pay on wine and blubber-fish; the emperor's men pay at Christmas and Easter two grey cloths and one brown, ten pounds of pepper, five pairs of gloves and two kegs of vinegar
entries.note: Undated; usually put about 1000 (?). Men of Huy, Liège and Nivelles pay toll as they pass through.

entries.title: Sea battle of Svolder: Olaf Tryggvason is beaten by the kings of the Danes and Svear and Jarl Eiríkr, and leaps from his ship
entries.place: Svolder (in the western Baltic, place unknown)
entries.effect: Norway shared out under the Danish king and the jarls of Lade
entries.note: The year is Ari's; 9 September is the later Icelandic tradition. Adam puts the battle in the Øresund.

entries.title: St Brice's Day: King Æthelred orders all the Danish men in England killed; at Oxford they are burned in St Frideswide's church
entries.effect: Danish traders in England killed or fled; Sweyn Forkbeard's revenge raids follow (1003)
entries.note: The charter S 909 (1004) tells of the burning at Oxford. That year the army had been paid 24,000 pounds.

entries.title: Northmen sail up the Waal and burn Tiel; at Utrecht the people burn their own trading quarter rather than leave it to them
sources: Alpert of Metz, De diversitate temporum i
entries.effect: Tiel, the new port of the Rhine delta, burned; traiectum's trading quarter burned
entries.note: Tiel took over much of Dorestad's trade in the 10th century (?).

entries.title: Æthelred pays the Danish army 36,000 pounds to leave
entries.effect: a great tribute in silver: English pennies go north in huge numbers

entries.title: 'Thorkell's army' lands at Sandwich; East Kent pays 3,000 pounds; the army winters on the Thames and raids all the south
entries.effect: raids across southern England for three years; the new English fleet of 1009 has come to nothing
entries.note: 'Soon after Lammas'.

entries.title: The Danish army kills Archbishop Ælfheah at Greenwich; 48,000 pounds of tribute is paid
entries.effect: a great tribute: the army breaks up; Thorkell and 45 ships take service with Æthelred
entries.note: Canterbury had been taken in September 1011. He refused to be ransomed and was pelted with bones at a feast.

entries.title: Sweyn Forkbeard conquers England: the north submits at Gainsborough, then Oxford, Winchester and London; Æthelred flees to Normandy
entries.effect: a Danish king of England: the English and Danish markets under one ruler
entries.note: Æthelred went to Normandy at Christmas.

entries.title: Sweyn Forkbeard dies at Gainsborough; the fleet chooses his son Cnut as king, but the English send for Æthelred
entries.effect: England at war again; Harald, Sweyn's other son, king of the Danes
entries.note: Candlemas.

entries.title: Battle of Clontarf: Brian Boru's army defeats the Leinstermen, the Dublin Norse and their allies from the isles; Brian and Sigurd of Orkney are killed
entries.effect: many Norse of the isles and Dublin killed; Dublin stays a Norse town under Sihtric, trading for the Irish kings
entries.note: Good Friday.

entries.title: The great sea-flood: on Michaelmas eve the sea runs further inland than ever before, drowning many villages and countless people
entries.effect: storm surge on the English coast: low ports, salt-pans and marsh pastures drowned

entries.title: Yaroslav gives the men of Novgorod a written law, the oldest part of the Russkaya Pravda (traditional date)
entries.effect: law: fixed fines (in marten skins and silver) in Novgorod and its lands, Varangians and townsmen alike
entries.note: The Novgorod chronicle ties the law to 1016; its date is debated.

entries.title: Battle of Assandun: Cnut defeats Edmund Ironside; they share England, and on Edmund's death (30 November) Cnut becomes king of all England
entries.effect: a Danish king of England: London and the North Sea ports under Cnut
entries.note: Æthelred had died in London on 23 April 1016.

entries.title: Cnut takes a tribute of 72,000 pounds from England and 10,500 from London, pays off his army and sends most of the fleet home, keeping forty ships
entries.effect: the greatest tribute of all: English silver floods into Denmark; a standing tax (heregeld) for the king's ships
entries.note: Cnut became king of the Danes too in 1018-1019.

entries.title: Battle of Vlaardingen: Count Dirk III of West Frisia beats the emperor's army sent to stop his toll on the Merwede, where the Tiel merchants pass
sources: Alpert of Metz, De diversitate temporum ii.20-21
entries.effect: a count's toll at the river mouth: ships to and from Tiel and Utrecht pay at Vlaardingen; the county of Holland grows from it
entries.note: The merchants of Tiel had complained to the emperor.

entries.title: The merchants of Tiel live by their own law: they claim an imperial charter to judge their own cases, and swear and drink together
sources: Alpert of Metz, De diversitate temporum ii.20
entries.effect: a merchants' guild on the Waal: Tiel the chief port of the Rhine delta, trading with England
entries.note: Alpert wrote about 1021-1024 and disapproved of them. London's laws of about 1000 (IV Æthelred) already name the emperor's men.

entries.title: Norsemen cut wood with iron tools at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland (dated to the year)
sources: dendrochronology and the cosmic-ray event of 993 (Kuitems et al. 2021)
entries.effect: evidence of the Norse in America: the camp is used only a few years
entries.note: The first exact year for Europeans in the Americas.

entries.title: Cnut at Rome for Conrad II's crowning wins lower tolls and safe passage for English and Danish merchants and pilgrims on the roads to Rome
entries.effect: law: Cnut's men, merchants and pilgrims pay fewer tolls at the Alpine passes and the Burgundian road
entries.note: Easter Day. The letter says the emperor, the pope, King Rudolf and the princes agreed to it.

entries.title: Cnut sails to Norway with fifty ships, drives out King Olaf Haraldsson and is taken as king
entries.effect: one king over England, Denmark and Norway: the North Sea at peace under Cnut

entries.title: Battle of Stiklestad: Olaf Haraldsson, back from Russia, is killed by the farmers' army; soon he is held a saint
entries.effect: Cnut's son Sweyn rules Norway; pilgrims begin to come to Nidaros (Trondheim)
entries.note: Sighvatr's poem tells of the sun darkening, usually taken as the eclipse of 31 August 1030.

entries.title: The caliphate of Cordoba is abolished; al-Andalus breaks up into the taifa kingdoms
entries.effect: al-Andalus split among small kingdoms: Seville, Toledo, Zaragoza, Denia, Almeria each with its own port and coin

entries.title: Cnut dies at Shaftesbury; his empire breaks up among his sons
entries.effect: Harold Harefoot in England, Harthacnut in Denmark, Magnus Olafsson already king in Norway (1035)

entries.title: Harthacnut dies at a wedding feast at Lambeth; Edward, son of Æthelred, is chosen king
entries.effect: an English king again; the paid fleet (lithsmen) kept on for a while
entries.note: 'As he stood at his drink.' Edward was crowned at Easter 1043.

entries.title: The last Rus attack on Constantinople, under Vladimir son of Yaroslav, is beaten with Greek fire and storms
entries.effect: Rus merchants expelled from Constantinople until the peace of about 1046
entries.note: It began with a quarrel in which a Rus merchant was killed.

entries.title: Battle of Lyrskov Heath near Hedeby: King Magnus of Norway and Denmark crushes a great army of Wends
entries.effect: the Wendish raids on Jutland stopped; Magnus also burns Jomsborg (Wolin) that year
entries.note: Michaelmas eve. The site is usually put at Lürschau, north of Schleswig (?).

entries.title: Magnus the Good dies; Harald Hardrada, back from the Varangian Guard with great wealth, rules Norway alone, Sweyn Estridsen Denmark
entries.effect: war between Norway and Denmark for seventeen years: Danish coasts raided, ports burned
entries.note: The day is the later saga tradition.

entries.title: Harald Hardrada burns Hedeby from end to end
entries.effect: sliesthorp burned: its trade shifts across the Schlei to Schleswig
entries.note: Dated 1049 or 1050 from the skalds' verses; the archaeology agrees that Hedeby declined in the 11th century.

entries.title: Cardinal Humbert lays a bull excommunicating Patriarch Michael Keroularios on the altar of Hagia Sophia; the churches of Rome and Constantinople split
entries.effect: news only: the Latin and Greek churches estranged; Latin merchants' churches at Constantinople closed

entries.title: Edward the Confessor dies; Harold Godwinson is crowned king the next day
entries.effect: a new king: Duke William of Normandy and Harald Hardrada both claim England; ships and men gathered all summer

entries.title: A great comet (Halley's comet) seen for a week from 24 April
entries.effect: news only: an omen everywhere; men wonder what it foretells
entries.note: 'On the eve of the Greater Litany'.

entries.title: After the Obodrite prince Gottschalk is killed, the Slavs rise, burn Hamburg and sack Schleswig
entries.effect: raid on sliesthorp: the old town finished; Schleswig on the north shore carries on its trade
entries.note: Gottschalk was killed on 7 June 1066.

entries.title: Harald Hardrada and Tostig beat the northern earls at Fulford, then are killed by King Harold at Stamford Bridge; 24 ships of 300 take the survivors home
entries.effect: eoforwic gave hostages to the Norwegians after Fulford; no Norse king tries to conquer England again
entries.note: Fulford was on 20 September.

entries.title: Duke William of Normandy lands at Pevensey and builds a castle at Hastings
sources: William of Poitiers, Gesta Guillelmi ii
entries.effect: the Sussex coast ravaged by the Norman army
entries.note: Michaelmas eve. The fleet had waited at Saint-Valery-sur-Somme for a wind.

entries.title: Battle of Hastings: King Harold is killed and the English army destroyed by Duke William
sources: William of Poitiers, Gesta Guillelmi ii
entries.effect: England open to the Normans: Dover and Canterbury submit; London holds out until December

entries.title: William of Normandy crowned king of England at Westminster on Christmas Day
sources: William of Poitiers, Gesta Guillelmi ii
entries.effect: England joined to Normandy: its trade turns towards Rouen and France; the end of the Viking Age in England
